articles.title: Navigating the Pancreatic Duct: Up-to-Date Radiologic Expedition through Intraluminal Pathologic Entities.
articles.abstract: Several congenital, traumatic, infectious, inflammatory, and neoplastic processes, as well as iatrogenic interventions, can alter intraluminal contents of the pancreatic duct, leading to adverse outcomes. Variant ductal anatomy may result in clinically significant complications such as duodenal obstruction, acute and chronic pancreatitis, and increased risk of developing gallbladder or biliary malignancies. The presence of calculi, blood, pus, and other unintended iatrogenic material in the pancreatic duct can be associated with a range of complications. Neoplastic involvement of the pancreatic duct by entities other than ductal adenocarcinoma is uncommon but may occur secondary to tumor extension into the duct or de novo development. CT and MRI or MR cholangiopancreatography are the most commonly used imaging modalities for evaluating the pancreatic duct and associated pathologic processes. Endoscopic US and endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography are more invasive imaging options that also provide the option of simultaneous intervention, if needed. The authors include discussion of the imaging appearances of various congenital anomalies and pathologic processes of the pancreatic duct and complications of ductal disruption and abnormal intraluminal contents. The section on neoplasia provides an up-to-date review of imaging manifestations of recently described neoplastic entities that develop within the pancreatic duct. Awareness of these abnormalities and their imaging correlates may help radiologists improve patient care.

articles.title: Advanced CT Myelography for Spontaneous Cerebrospinal Fluid Leaks.
articles.abstract: Spontaneous intracranial hypotension is a frequently debilitating condition that is most commonly caused by loss of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) from the spine. The most frequently occurring types of spontaneous spinal CSF leaks that cause spontaneous intracranial hypotension are ventral dural tears, lateral dural tears, and CSF venous fistulas, but other leak types are recognized including sacral dural tears or fistulas into vascular malformations. Localization and characterization of spinal CSF leaks with CT myelography facilitates subsequent targeted treatment. A tailored approach based on the suspected leak type as determined at MRI of the spine is necessary to maximize the likelihood of a diagnostic study. The authors focus primarily on advanced CT myelographic techniques for leaks from dural tears and CSF venous fistulas. The importance of optimal patient positioning, typical and atypical appearances of the different leak types, and artifacts that can mimic a CSF leak are considered. ©RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See the invited commentary by Madhavan in this issue.

articles.title: The evolution of image-guided ablations for thyroid disorders: a historical review.
articles.abstract: Over the past four decades, the management of thyroid nodules and selected thyroid malignancies has progressively shifted from surgery-centered approaches toward image-guided minimally invasive treatments (MITT). What began in 1985 with ultrasound-guided percutaneous ethanol injection evolved into a range of energy-based techniques, including laser ablation (LA), radiofrequency ablation (RFA), microwave ablation (MWA), and high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU).This historical review aimed to reconstruct the major milestones in the development of image-guided thyroid ablation. A systematic PubMed literature search and predefined selection criteria were used to identify seminal studies, first clinical applications, major technological innovations, comparative studies, guideline-defining publications, and landmark long-term follow-up studies. Overall, 43 milestone papers were included for qualitative historical analysis. The evolution of thyroid ablation can be divided into five phases: conceptual origins (1985-1999), birth of the thermal procedures' era (2000-2006), methodological standardization (2007-2012), oncologic consolidation and comparative evidence (2013-2018), and final codification by means of international guideline endorsement and long-term validation (2019-2025). Recent 10-year follow-up studies have confirmed the durable efficacy of MITT for benign nodule management and their sustained oncologic control in low-risk papillary thyroid microcarcinoma. Image-guided thyroid ablation has transitioned from experimental innovation to an evidence-based, guideline-supported therapeutic domain, representing a paradigm shift toward precision medicine, organ preservation, and minimally invasive endocrine oncology.

articles.title: TheraPb Phase 1b: First-in-Human Dose-Escalation and Optimization Study of 212Pb-ADVC001 in PSMA-Positive Metastatic Androgen Pathway Modulation-Resistant Prostate Cancer.
articles.abstract: [212Pb]Pb-ADVC001 (212Pb-ADVC001) is a prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy with high linear energy transfer derived predominantly from the alpha-emission of its 212Pb payload which, upon decay, delivers potent ionizing radiation directly to the tumor. TheraPb (NCT05720130) is a first-in-human dose-escalation and optimization study evaluating 212Pb-ADVC001 in metastatic androgen pathway modulation-resistant prostate cancer (mAPM-R, formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer). Phase 1 results, including available long-term safety and efficacy outcomes, are presented. Methods: Participants with progressive mAPM-R previously treated with ≥1 androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor and ≥1 taxane chemotherapy (unless contraindicated/declined) were enrolled. Escalating doses of 60-200 MBq 212Pb-ADVC001 were administered at prespecified intervals every 6, 4, 2, or 1 week(s) for up to 6 doses across 7 dose-schedule cohorts (interval 3 + 3 design). The primary objective was to determine the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) with primary endpoints of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) and adverse events (AEs). Secondary endpoints included prostate-specific antigen (PSA) response, overall response rate (ORR), and radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS). Results: Twenty-two participants were enrolled, with a median follow-up of 14.1 months (IQR 8.8-17.1). No DLTs were observed and the maximum tolerated dose was not reached. The most common treatment-related AEs (TRAE) were dry mouth (18/22 participants [82%], all grade 1-2) and nausea (14/22 participants [64%], all grade 1-2); there were no grade 4-5 or serious TRAEs. The selected RP2D are 160 and 200 MBq. At these dose levels, 12/15 (80%) participants had a PSA decline of ≥50% and the median rPFS from C1D1 was 11.2 months (95% CI 2.0-not estimable) as of data cutoff. ORR was 100%, with centrally confirmed objective responses in all 5 Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours (RECIST)-evaluable participants treated at the RP2D. Conclusion: 212Pb-ADVC001 was well tolerated up to 200 MBq, including at weekly dosing, and showed encouraging anti-tumor activity in pretreated mAPM-R. Two RP2D, 160 and 200 MBq, are under evaluation in phase 2.

articles.title: Predictive and operational artificial intelligence in emergency radiology for early risk stratification in acute care settings: a scoping review.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Emergency departments face increasing overcrowding, resulting in diagnostic delays, higher mortality, and rising healthcare costs. Early risk stratification is essential to optimise clinical decision-making. Although medical imaging plays a central role in initial assessment, workload pressures and operational constraints have driven the development of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support triage and prioritisation in emergency radiology. OBJECTIVE: To map and synthesise evidence on the applications, performance, and limitations of AI in emergency radiology for early risk stratification in acute care. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines and Joanna Briggs Institute recommendations. The protocol was developed a priori and registered in the Open Science Framework. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated AI applications in medical imaging in acute care settings. Evidence was synthesised using conceptual mapping and thematic analysis. RESULTS: Seventy-one studies were included. Computed tomography was the most frequently evaluated modality, followed by radiography and ultrasound. Major domains included neurovascular disease, acute cardiopulmonary conditions, trauma, COVID-19, and acute aortic syndromes. Studies reported high diagnostic performance and potential workflow benefits; however, evidence was predominantly retrospective and internally validated, with limited prospective evaluation, external validation, or evidence of improved patient-level outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: AI applications in emergency radiology show promising diagnostic and workflow-support capabilities. However, current evidence largely reflects early-stage development, with limited prospective validation, scarce real-world impact assessment, and insufficient evaluation of clinically meaningful outcomes. KEY POINTS: Question How clinically mature are AI applications designed to support early risk stratification and prioritisation in time-sensitive emergency radiology workflows? Findings Most studies report high diagnostic performance in time-sensitive conditions, yet evidence remains predominantly retrospective with limited external validation or prospective real-world implementation. Clinical relevance AI may support earlier identification and prioritisation of critical imaging findings, but routine adoption requires prospective external validation and evidence of meaningful effects on clinical decisions and patient outcomes.

articles.title: From dusk till dawn?-Night shift-induced fatigue, diagnostic performance, and AI assistance in chest radiography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of night shift-induced fatigue on radiology residents' diagnostic performance and to assess whether AI assistance offsets potential performance loss. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective intra-individual reader study, ten radiology residents (mean experience: 35 months; three women) interpreted three sets of 33 chest radiographs before and after a first-call on-site night shift. Sessions included two pre-shift readings (morning/afternoon, without AI) and two post-shift readings (morning, with/without AI). Eye tracking captured fixation duration and saccade count, and fatigue was defined as a ≥ 5% reduction in the slope of the saccadic main sequence between pre- and post-shift sessions. Diagnostic accuracy (Cohen's κ vs. expert majority vote), efficiency (mean reporting time per radiograph), eye-tracking metrics, and user surveys were analyzed with generalized linear mixed models and post-hoc Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons. RESULTS: Six of ten radiology residents were classified as fatigued, among whom diagnostic accuracy declined significantly post-shift (from κ = 0.71 ± 0.05 to κ = 0.61 ± 0.10; p < 0.001), with reduced fixation duration (p = 0.010) and saccade count (p = 0.015). Non-fatigued readers showed a smaller decline in accuracy (from κ = 0.72 ± 0.03 to κ = 0.65 ± 0.03; p = 0.037). Reporting times remained stable pre- and post-shift (p ≥ 0.463). AI assistance did not significantly improve diagnostic accuracy (Δκ = 0.03-0.04; p ≥ 0.525). Reporting times were numerically shorter with AI assistance in fatigued readers (Δ6.3 s; p = 0.122) and significantly shorter in non-fatigued readers (Δ9.9 s; p = 0.031). Surveys indicated mental exhaustion and reduced focus in fatigued readers. CONCLUSION: Night-shift-induced fatigue impaired diagnostic accuracy without slowing reporting speed, raising patient safety concerns. The utilized AI model did not restore pre-shift performance. KEY POINTS: Question Night-shift-induced fatigue may reduce diagnostic accuracy of radiology residents in chest radiography, yet its objective quantification and the compensatory potential of AI assistance remain unclear. Findings Fatigue, based on eye-tracking measurements of oculomotor efficiency, reduced diagnostic accuracy after night shifts without slowing reporting speed; AI assistance did not significantly improve accuracy. Clinical relevance Night-shift-induced fatigue can lower diagnostic accuracy in chest radiography despite unchanged reporting speed, posing patient-safety risks. The AI model used in this study cannot fully compensate for fatigue-related performance decline.

articles.title: CT features of extra-pancreatic nerve plexus invasion predict mortality in early-stage pancreatic cancer.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The presence of extra-pancreatic nerve plexus invasion (EPNI) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is known to correlate with aggressive disease, however, it is unknown whether specific pathways or morphologies carry different prognostic implications. This study evaluates whether distinct CT-defined patterns of EPNI predict mortality in PDAC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 89 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC who underwent preoperative pancreatic protocol multidetector CT (MDCT) followed by surgical resection. Patients were identified from an institutional database and required available preoperative CT and histopathology. Two blinded, experienced radiologists reviewed MDCT images to assess EPNI, which was categorized by anatomic pathway and morphologic pattern. Overall survival was compared between EPNI-positive and EPNI-negative groups and among EPNI subtypes using log-rank testing, with stratification by tumor stage. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, and surgical margin were performed. RESULTS: A total of 89 patients (M/F: 54/35), median age: 66 years (IQR, 60-70 years), were evaluated. CT evidence of EPNI was present in 65 patients (73%) and was associated with decreased overall survival (p < 0.001). This association remained significant in Stage I tumors (p < 0.001). PPC2 pathway involvement (p < 0.001) and mass-with-stranding morphology (p < 0.001) were each associated with reduced overall survival. PPC2 (p = 0.003) and mass-with-stranding (p < 0.001) remained significant in stage I tumors. CONCLUSION: Preoperative CT detection of EPNI, especially PPC2 pathway involvement and mass-with-stranding morphology, identifies high-risk PDAC patients. KEY POINTS: Question Extra pancreatic nerve plexus invasion in pancreatic adenocarcinoma is associated with aggressive disease, but the prognostic significance of specific pathways or morphologies remains unknown. Findings Plexus pancreaticus capitalis 2 involvement and mass-with-stranding morphology in EPNI of pancreatic adenocarcinoma are associated with decreased overall survival. Clinical relevance Identifying high-risk EPNI features on CT may facilitate early prognostic stratification and inform surgical and neoadjuvant treatment planning in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

articles.title: Timeliness of an Expedited Diagnostic Pathway for Screening Mammography Recalls.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare diagnostic and biopsy timeliness, malignancy yield, and cancer characteristics between expedited and standard screening mammography recall pathways. METHODS: An expedited recall workflow implemented in Epic enabled radiologists to flag highly suspicious BI-RADS 0 findings for telephone scheduling into reserved appointments, targeting diagnostic evaluation within one week. We retrospectively reviewed recalls from 11/1/2024-1/31/2026. Primary outcomes were time from screening to diagnostic evaluation and malignancy yield (PPV1 and PPV3). Secondary outcomes included diagnostic-to-biopsy and screening-to-biopsy intervals, delayed diagnostic imaging (≥30 days from screening), delayed biopsy (≥30 days from diagnostic), and malignancy characteristics. Intervals were measured in calendar days. RESULTS: Among 36,384 screening mammograms, 4,647 were BI-RADS 0 (recall rate 12.8%); 57 (1.2%) were expedited. After excluding 247 standard pathway cases without follow-up, 4,400 were analyzed. Expedited patients were older (median 64.6 vs 52.5 years, p<0.001) with shorter median screening-to-diagnostic (7 vs 25 days), diagnostic-to-biopsy (14 vs 19 days), and screening-to-biopsy intervals (24 vs 45 days; all p<0.001). Delayed diagnostic imaging (7.0% vs 38.2%, p<0.001) and biopsy (1.8% vs 14.5%, p=0.004) were less frequent. Expedited cases had higher BI-RADS 4/5 rates (96.5% vs 30.1%, p<0.001) and malignancy yield (PPV1 91.2% vs 5.2%; PPV3 94.5% vs 18.2%; p<0.001). Multivariable logistic regression among 278 cancers identified mass findings (OR 3.36, p<0.001) and imaging size (OR 1.03/mm, p=0.003) as predictors of expedited routing. DISCUSSION: Radiologists identified highly suspicious screening mammography findings for expedited evaluation. Expedited routing was associated with shorter diagnostic and biopsy intervals and high malignancy yield, supporting diagnostic resource prioritization.

articles.title: Prognostic Value of 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 uPAR PET/CT in Resected Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Single-Center Prospective Study.
articles.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer shows wide variability in outcomes after curative-intent resection. 18F-FDG PET/CT is indispensable for staging but primarily reflects glucose metabolism rather than the invasion-related tumor biology that may contribute to recurrence. 68Ga-NOTA-AE105 PET/CT images the urokinase-type plasminogen activator receptor (uPAR), a cell-surface mediator of local invasion and metastatic spread. We assessed whether preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT is prognostic for postoperative recurrence. Methods: We conducted a single-center cohort study of patients with resectable lung adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma who were prospectively enrolled to undergo preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET/CT in addition to standard-of-care 18F-FDG PET/CT. Primary tumor SUVmean and SUVmax were measured for both tracers, and tumor tissue uPAR expression was quantified by immunohistochemistry (H-score). Postoperative recurrence was the primary endpoint and was analyzed in a competing-risks framework with death as a competing event. The primary prognostic analyses evaluated 68Ga-uPAR SUVs, 18F-FDG SUVs, and uPAR H-score as continuous variables using univariable cause-specific Cox models. A 1.5-y horizon was used for exploratory Youden-derived high versus low groups, for which cumulative incidence of recurrence was estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Trial registration number is NCT02755675 Results: Thirty-seven patients comprised the analysis cohort, of whom 14 developed recurrence during a median follow-up of 2.38 y (interquartile range, 1.97-8.20 y). Four patients died without prior recurrence. 68Ga-uPAR uptake correlated with tumor tissue uPAR expression, whereas 18F-FDG uptake did not. As continuous prognostic factors, higher 68Ga-uPAR SUVmax (hazard ratio, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.34-3.49; P = 0.002) and higher uPAR H-score (hazard ratio, 1.04 per unit; 95% CI, 1.01-1.08; P = 0.017) were associated with recurrence; 68Ga-uPAR SUVmean showed borderline evidence of association (P = 0.053), whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic. Exploratory 1.5-y threshold analyses showed greater early recurrence in the high SUVmean and high H-score groups; the SUVmax comparison did not reach statistical significance. Conclusion: Preoperative 68Ga-uPAR PET uptake reflected tumor uPAR expression and was associated with early postoperative recurrence, whereas 18F-FDG uptake was not prognostic in this cohort. These findings suggest that uPAR PET captures invasion-related tumor biology that is not fully reflected by glucose metabolism imaging. External validation is required.

articles.title: Delta-like Ligand 3-Targeted Imaging in Small Cell Lung Cancer.
Head-to-Head Comparison of 18F-SynVest-1 PET and 18F-FDG PET in the Differentiation of Patients with Cognitive Decline.
articles.abstract: Although 18F-FDG PET is commonly used in the differential diagnosis of cognitive decline, synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A PET may offer a more direct assessment of synaptic integrity and address limitations associated with 18F-FDG, such as sensitivity to sensory stimuli and glycemic variations. In this study, a head-to-head comparison of 18F-SynVesT-1 and 18F-FDG was performed for differentiating causes of cognitive decline in a tertiary clinical setting. Methods: Patients with cognitive decline referred for 18F-FDG PET were recruited to undergo 18F-SynVesT-1 PET/MRI (49 ± 26 d after 18F-FDG PET). Diagnosis was determined by routine clinical follow-up (median, 11 mo) and classified as Alzheimer disease (AD), frontotemporal degeneration (FTD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), other neurodegenerative disorders (ONDs), or nonneurodegenerative disorders (NoNDs). Volume-wise and voxelwise semiquantitative analyses were performed using tracer-specific healthy volunteers. Diagnostic accuracy for both tracers was evaluated through logistic regression and by consensus from 3 readers. Noninferiority was defined by an area-under-the-curve margin (ΔAUC) of -0.10 within a 95% CI, using the clinical follow-up diagnosis as the gold standard. Results: Ninety-four patients were included: 44 with AD, 12 with FTD, 4 with DLB, 5 with ONDs, and 29 with NoNDs. Volume-wise and voxelwise analyses showed that, in patients with AD and DLB, reductions in the temporoparietal and precuneus/posterior cingulate were less pronounced with 18F-SynVesT-1 PET than with 18F-FDG PET (e.g., posterior cingulate in AD, -10% vs. -20%). In FTD, the most impacted areas showed greater variability, typically affecting the anterior temporal and frontal cortices, depending on the FTD subtype. Visual assessment showed lower sensitivity for AD with 18F-SynVesT-1 PET than with 18F-FDG PET (0.57 vs. 0.73) with equal specificity (0.76), whereas quantitative analysis yielded a lower area under the curve (0.71 vs. 0.81; ΔAUC, -0.10; 95% CI, -0.21 to 0.01). For FTD, 18F-SynVesT-1 visual classification yielded similar sensitivity and specificity (0.58 and 0.90) compared with 18F-FDG (0.50 and 0.93) but a lower quantitative area under the curve (0.64 vs. 0.76; ΔAUC, -0.12; 95% CI, -0.27 to 0.04). Conclusion: 18F-SynVesT-1 PET enabled accurate classification of disease-specific patterns of cognitive decline. Although classification performance for FTD was similar to that of 18F-FDG PET, the lower effect size in neocortical binding resulted in lower sensitivity for AD. Larger study samples are needed to formally evaluate tracer noninferiority in this clinical context for all subgroups.

articles.title: [18F]DOPA PET Reveals Metabolically Active Transcriptomic States Associated with Clinical Outcome in Pancreatic Neuroendocrine Tumors.
articles.abstract: [18F]fluorodihydroxyphenylalanine ([18F]DOPA) uptake is dependent on amino acid transport and decarboxylation pathways, including large neutral amino acid transporter 1, encoded by SLC7A5, which are linked to tumor aggressiveness. This study evaluated whether in vivo uptake of [18F]DOPA can serve as an imaging biomarker for pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (panNETs), reflecting a tumor's transcriptional status and a patient's clinical course. Methods: This retrospective single-center study was based on a transcriptomic cohort of 74 primary panNETs. A subset of 22 panNETs from patients who underwent preoperative [18F]DOPA PET/CT constituted the discovery radiotranscriptomic cohort. [18F]DOPA tumor uptake was quantified using SUVmax and integrated with matched RNA-sequencing data. Unsupervised clustering, differential expression analysis, gene set enrichment, and tumor microenvironment deconvolution were performed to identify transcriptional programs associated with [18F]DOPA uptake. The prognostic value of SLC7A5 was evaluated in the discovery cohort, the full transcriptomic cohort (n = 74), and an independent external cohort (n = 33). Results: Unsupervised clustering of gene expression profiles identified 2 robust molecular subtypes: cluster 1 and cluster 2. Cluster 1 showed higher [18F]DOPA uptake than did cluster 2, with a median SUVmax of 24.3 versus 5.9, respectively (P = 0.030), and was associated with more advanced clinicopathologic features and shorter event-free survival. This subtype was also characterized by enrichment in extracellular matrix, stromal, vascular, and immune-related components, along with upregulation of amino acid transport and amine metabolism genes, including SLC7A5 As a mechanistic link between tracer uptake and tumor metabolism, SLC7A5 expression significantly stratified event-free survival in the discovery cohort and remained prognostic in the full cohort. Conclusion: [18F]DOPA PET uptake was associated with amino acid-driven metabolic programs in panNETs, including SLC7A5 expression, and adverse clinical features. These findings suggest that [18F]DOPA uptake may provide a noninvasive readout of tumor metabolic activity, although its value as an imaging biomarker requires independent validation.

articles.title: Targeted α-Therapy with 211At-Labeled Trastuzumab Overcomes Trastuzumab Resistance in Uterine Serous Carcinoma in Mice.
articles.abstract: Uterine serous carcinoma (USC) is an aggressive endometrial cancer frequently associated with human epidermal growth factor receptor type 2 (HER2) overexpression and poor prognosis. Although trastuzumab improves outcomes, resistance remains a major clinical problem. This study determined whether targeted α-therapy using 211At-labeled trastuzumab (211At-trastuzumab) can overcome trastuzumab resistance in HER2-positive USC. Methods: 211At-trastuzumab was synthesized, and its binding and cytotoxicity in HER2-positive USC cell lines were evaluated. Three trastuzumab-resistant peritoneal metastasis mouse models were established: intrinsic resistance, trastuzumab-induced resistance, and acquired resistance. After a single intravenous administration (1.85 MBq), therapeutic efficacy was assessed using bioluminescence imaging and biodistribution analysis. Results: 211At-trastuzumab showed specific binding to HER2-positive USC cells and significantly reduced cell viability relative to the controls. In vivo, tumor uptake reached 17.4 ± 1.9 %ID/g at 24 h. A single dose significantly suppressed tumor growth in all 3 resistant models: intrinsic, induced, and acquired resistance (P < 0.05 vs. controls). No severe toxicity was observed. Conclusion: 211At-trastuzumab demonstrates potent antitumor efficacy against trastuzumab-resistant HER2-positive USC in preclinical models. Targeted α-therapy may represent a promising strategy to overcome resistance to HER2-targeted therapy.

articles.title: Is 186/188Re Really Happening?
Clinical Value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT Versus [18F]FDG PET/CT for Primary Staging of Gastroesophageal Adenocarcinoma: Results from a Prospective Northern European Trial.
articles.abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated promising results for radiolabeled fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET/CT in gastric cancer (GC) when compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT. In this prospective clinical trial, we assessed the impact of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT compared with [18F]FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) on primary staging and management of Danish patients with GC and gastroesophageal junction cancer (GEJC). Methods: Between February 8, 2024, and September 26, 2025, consecutive patients with GC or GEJC who were candidates for surgical resection and perioperative chemotherapy were included in this trial. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT images were deidentified and presented to the treating clinicians after the trial, at which point [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET/CT-based staging and tentative patient management were determined. Results: Twenty patients were included in the trial, including 15 (75%) with GEJC and 5 (25%) with GC; all patients were diagnosed with adenocarcinoma. For the primary tumor, [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 and [18F]FDG PET/CT agreed in 18 (90%) of cases, and both modalities demonstrated a detection rate of 90% (95% CI, 68%-99%). For clinical nodal staging, ceCT detected more lymph nodes than did [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and [18F]FDG PET alone (81 vs. 53 vs. 44, respectively). [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET did not detect additional lymph nodes beyond those detected with ceCT. Despite detecting fewer lymph nodes overall, [18F]FDG PET identified 6 additional lymph nodes in 5 patients, resulting in clinical nodal upstaging in 4 cases (20%) compared with both [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET and ceCT. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET would have led to clinical metastatic upstaging in 4 patients (20%) because of the identification of potential distant metastases (1 peritoneal and 3 liver metastases), which would have resulted in a change in recommended patient management from curative-intent to palliative treatment in 3 patients (15%). Conclusion: The primary clinical value of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET was its ability to detect distant metastases that were negative on [18F]FDG PET and ceCT, potentially impacting patient management. There were no obvious advantages in the evaluation of primary tumor and regional lymph nodes. Although the study population is relatively small and mostly consists of patients with GEJC, this study represents the first prospective investigation of consecutive patients in a well-defined, clinical northern European setting and indicates potential future roles for [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-46 PET in GC and GEJC.

articles.title: Preclinical PET Imaging of Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in Tumors with Heterogeneous HER2 Expression.
articles.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has clinical activity in human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-low and -ultralow tumors in addition to HER2-positive tumors. However, no consistent correlation has been observed between traditional HER2 scoring criteria and response to T-DXd in HER2-low and HER2-ultralow tumors. There is a need for complementary approaches to monitor T-DXd delivery in vivo and potentially improve understanding of which tumors may benefit from T-DXd therapy. This study evaluated tumor uptake of radiolabeled T-DXd in tumors with varying HER2 protein levels using PET in treatment-naïve tumors and during T-DXd therapy. Methods: Chelator-conjugated T-DXd or trastuzumab was prepared via conventional lysine conjugation and radiolabeled with 64Cu. The binding and in vitro cytotoxicity of the conjugates were determined in cancer cell lines. PET/CT was performed across 11 tumor models (representing 5 tumor types), including cell xenografts, patient-derived xenografts, and syngeneic models in both subcutaneous and orthotopic models. Image-based tumor uptake of the radiolabeled antibodies was quantified in all models. In the treatment studies, mice bearing CT26-hHER2 tumors that express heterogeneous HER2 with an immunohistochemistry score of 2+ levels received weekly coinjections of therapeutic T-DXd (6 mg/kg) together with imaging-dose [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd (4 mg/kg), corresponding to a total T-DXd administered dose of 10 mg/kg. Results: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd was obtained at a radiochemical purity of at least 98%. Purified [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd bound to cells in a concentration-dependent manner and had a positive correlation between HER2 protein levels and bound T-DXd. Conjugation of T-DXd to NOTA did not affect T-DXd binding or cytotoxicity in cancer cells. [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd mean tumor uptake varied across models (7.45 ± 1.28 to 19.10 ± 2.50 %ID/mL), and the mean uptake was similar to that of the parental antibody 64Cu-labeled trastuzumab. Preimaging doses of either trastuzumab or pertuzumab did not affect [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake in tumors. There was a positive correlation between the change in [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd uptake and the change in tumor volume between weeks 1 and 2 of T-DXd treatment (P < 0.01) in CT26.hHER2 tumors grown in immunocompetent mice. Conclusion: [64Cu]Cu-NOTA-T-DXd PET detects antibody-drug accumulation in tumors with low HER2 protein levels and may provide an early imaging biomarker associated with response. These studies show the potential of using HER2-targeted imaging in preclinical models to noninvasively assess antibody-drug conjugate delivery and explore imaging-based biomarkers associated with T-DXd response.

articles.title: LungCheck: Pilot Testing a Theory-Informed Multicomponent Strategy to Increase Lung Cancer Screening in Primary Care Settings.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) reduces lung cancer-specific and all-cause mortality, yet uptake remains low. This study evaluates LungCheck, a theory-informed multicomponent behavior change and implementation strategy designed to increase LDCT ordering in two diverse primary care settings. METHODS: This pilot study compared 16-month pilot and pre-pilot periods at a federally qualified health center (FQHC) and an academic faculty practice in New York City. LungCheck comprised educational meetings, materials and clinician reminders, an implementation blueprint, patient navigation, and EHR modifications. LDCT ordering rates (primary outcome) were compared using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Post-implementation surveys assessed acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. RESULTS: A total of 5,918 patient-period observations were included (1,569 academic; 4,349 FQHC). Among patients with documented LCS eligibility, the odds of LDCT ordering were significantly higher during the pilot at both the academic practice (OR, 2.67; 95% CI, 1.47-4.85; p=0.001) and FQHC (OR, 4.53; 95% CI, 2.29-8.94; p<0.001). A combined-site multivariable model adjusting for site, age, sex, and race confirmed higher odds of LDCT ordering during the pilot (OR, 1.95; 95% CI, 1.44-2.63; p<0.001). Among patients with an LDCT order, completion was 71.4% (10/14) pre-pilot versus 35.7% (15/42) during the pilot at the academic practice and 42.9% (18/42; 95% CI, 28%-59%) versus 39.3% (24/61; 95% CI, 27%-53%) at the FQHC. The strategy was rated as highly acceptable (AIM, 4.47/5), appropriate (IAM, 4.44/5), and feasible (FIM, 4.41/5). DISCUSSION: LungCheck was associated with significantly increased LDCT ordering at both sites, high acceptability, feasibility, and appropriateness ratings and high provider knowledge, confidence, and perceived skills related to LCS. Although a corresponding improvement in LDCT completion was not observed, the small number of LDCT orders limited the precision of completion estimates. Persistent environmental and patient-level barriers underscore the need to adapt LungCheck into a multilevel intervention addressing patient-, provider, and system-level barriers across the LCS continuum, to be evaluated in a future cluster randomized trial.

articles.title: Mapping International Lung Cancer Screening Quality Indicators to the American College of Radiology Lung Cancer Screening Registry: A Crosswalk Analysis.
articles.abstract: The International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) established 26 consensus quality indicators (QIs) for lung cancer screening (LCS) programs, of which 20 were rated as essential and 6 as desirable by the expert panel. We evaluated the extent to which the American College of Radiology (ACR) Lung Cancer Screening Registry (LCSR), the largest LCS registry in the U.S., can support measurement of the IASLC QIs. We performed a crosswalk analysis, mapping all 26 IASLC QIs to the LCSR Data Dictionary and its 46 clinical performance measures, classifying each as directly measurable, derivable, or not measurable. The crosswalk was reviewed and independently validated by members of the ACR Early Lung Cancer Detection Registry Quality and Education Committee. Eight QIs (30.8%) were directly measurable, 10 (38.5%) were derivable, and 8 (30.8%) were not measurable from LCSR data alone. The LCSR therefore contains sufficient data elements to support measurement of approximately 69% of IASLC QIs. Remaining gaps involve screening uptake, clinical investigation, procedure complications, curative-intent treatment, treatment equity, diagnostic investigation equity and selected wait-time measures and would require additional registry fields or external data linkage.

articles.title: A Multilevel Intervention to Improve Lung Cancer Screening Among Hispanic Patients: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: We evaluated the preliminary efficacy of Empower LCS, a culturally-adapted multilevel intervention, compared with enhanced usual care (EUC) for improving LCS uptake among Hispanic patients. METHODS: In this pilot randomized controlled trial, Hispanic patients aged 50-80 years who met 2021 US Preventive Services Task Force LCS eligibility criteria were enrolled between February 2024 and August 2025. Participants were randomized 1:1 to EUC or Empower LCS. EUC included usual care plus a one-page educational handout. Empower LCS included a culturally adapted decision aid, provider notifications, patient text reminders, and health-related social needs support. The primary outcome was LDCT ordering within 4 months, assessed by medical record review or self-report. Analyses used chi-square tests and logistic regressions. RESULTS: Sixty patients were randomized (mean age, 60.8 years ± 7.4; 37/60 [61.7%] male; 21/60 [35.0%] Spanish-speaking). At 4 months, LDCT ordering was higher with Empower LCS than with EUC (15/30 [50.0%] vs 4/30 [13.3%]; p=0.002), as were LCS discussions (12/30 [40.0%] vs 5/30 [16.7%]; p=0.045). LDCT completion was higher but not significant (9/30 [30.0%] vs 4/30 [13.3%]; p=0.117), likely due to small sample size. In exploratory adjusted models, Empower LCS was associated with higher odds of LCS ordering (OR, 7.32; 95% CI, 1.97-34.16), and discussion (OR, 4.1; 95% CI, 1.20-16.28). Qualitative interviews identified provider trust and logistical barriers as drivers of screening engagement and completion, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Empower LCS increased LDCT ordering and screening discussions in this pilot trial. These findings support culturally tailored, low-cost, scalable interventions to reduce disparities in LCS participation.

Stochastic Siamese MAE Pretraining for Longitudinal Medical Images.
articles.abstract: Temporally aware image representations are crucial for capturing disease progression in 3D volumes of longitudinal medical datasets. However, recent state-of-the-art self-supervised learning approaches like Masked Autoencoding (MAE), despite their strong representation learning capabilities, lack temporal awareness. In this paper, we propose STAMP (Stochastic Temporal Autoencoder with Masked Pretraining), a Siamese MAE framework that encodes temporal information through a stochastic process by conditioning on the time difference between the 2 input volumes. Unlike deterministic Siamese approaches, which compare scans from different time points but fail to account for the inherent uncertainty in disease evolution, STAMP learns temporal dynamics stochastically by reframing the MAE reconstruction loss as a conditional variational inference objective. We evaluated STAMP on two OCT and one MRI datasets with multiple visits per patient. STAMP pretrained ViT models outperformed both existing temporal MAE methods and foundation models on different late stage Age-Related Macular Degeneration and Alzheimer's Disease progression prediction which require models to learn the underlying non-deterministic temporal dynamics of the diseases.

articles.title: The FIBR-CMR score: a novel risk model integrating fibrinogen and cardiac magnetic resonance for major adverse events after STEMI.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Survivors of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) face a substantial residual risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCEs). Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) excellently delineates structural injury but does not assess the concomitant systemic prothrombotic state. We investigated whether fibrinogen, a key mediator of thrombosis, provides incremental prognostic value beyond CMR for risk stratification. METHODS: In a prospective multicenter cohort of 532 STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), plasma fibrinogen was measured post-procedure. CMR was performed within 7 days to assess left ventricular thrombus (LVT) and aneurysm (LVA). The primary endpoint was MACCEs over a median follow-up of 55.5 months. A novel risk score (the Fibrinogen and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Score, or FIBR-CMR score) was derived from a multivariable Cox model, and its performance was assessed through internal validation using bootstrap resampling (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73). RESULTS: Elevated fibrinogen independently predicted LVT (adjusted OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.09-1.96) and LVA (adjusted OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.20-1.79) after adjusting for clinical and CMR confounders. Fibrinogen (≥ 3.36 g/L) independently predicted MACCEs (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.53), an effect partially mediated by LVT (48.5%) and LVA (38.0%). The FIBR-CMR score (1 point for elevated fibrinogen, 2 for LVT, 2 for LVA) stratified patients into low (0 points), intermediate (1-2 points), and high (≥ 3 points) risk groups. The high-risk group had a strikingly elevated 5-year MACCE incidence of 48.3%, compared to 15.2% and 6.0% in the intermediate- and low-risk groups, respectively (optimism-corrected C-index = 0.73). CONCLUSION: The integration of fibrinogen with CMR-defined structural injury provides powerful synergism for risk assessment. The FIBR-CMR score, derived from a prospective multicenter cohort, effectively identifies a high-risk phenotype of STEMI patients. This score now requires external validation but represents a promising step toward personalized risk assessment. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinicaltrials.gov; NCT03768453.

articles.title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF). METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory. RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively. CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

articles.title: The role of extracardiac radiotracer biodistribution in the evaluation of cardiac amyloidosis: a retrospective multicenter study on [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Bone scintigraphy using [99mTc]Tc-DPD or [99mTc]Tc-HMDP is a non-invasive cornerstone for diagnosing transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CA). However, their interchangeability and the clinical relevance of systemic extracardiac uptake (ExtCU) remain poorly defined. AIM: To systematically compare the diagnostic performance and whole-body biodistribution profiles of [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP in patients with suspected cardiac amyloidosis (CA). METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated a multicenter cohort of patients investigated for suspected CA who underwent late planar whole-body scintigraphy and targeted SPECT/CT with either radiotracer as part of their diagnostic workup. Inclusion required a final, confirmed diagnosis of ATTRwt, ATTRv, or AL amyloidosis. Myocardial visual Perugini score (VISUAL_PS) and systemic ExtCU (pulmonary, appendicular muscular, visceral, and miscellaneous) were recorded. RESULTS: The study included 224 patients (DPD: n = 109, comprising 70 ATTRwt, 20 ATTRv, 19 AL; HMDP: n = 115, comprising 90 ATTRwt, 13 ATTRv, 12 AL). In ATTRwt, the DPD cohort presented predominantly with Perugini Grade 2 (76%), whereas the HMDP cohort skewed toward Grade 3 (72%, p < 0.001). DPD was significantly associated with appendicular muscular uptake (ATTRwt: 84% vs. 38%, p < 0.001), creating a competitive "soft-tissue sink effect". Conversely, HMDP demonstrated a unique predilection for pulmonary retention (ATTRwt: 68% vs. 46%, p = 0.008; ATTRv: 61% vs. 10%, p = 0.006). Visceral uptake was rare in ATTR but was a robust negative predictor strongly favoring AL amyloidosis (OR 0.016, p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: [99mTc]Tc-DPD and [99mTc]Tc-HMDP possess distinct biodistribution profiles precluding direct interchangeability. HMDP maximizes myocardial contrast, whereas DPD provides a superior representation of the systemic musculoskeletal amyloid burden. Nuclear medicine physicians must adopt tracer-specific interpretive approaches to optimize non-invasive phenotyping. TRIAL REGISTRATION: not applicable.
articles.journal: Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

articles.title: Latent class analysis of CT-based phenotypes in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis and pulmonary involvement.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Pulmonary manifestations of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) are highly heterogeneous, and a standardized CT-based classification is currently lacking. This study aimed to evaluate whether latent class analysis (LCA) of chest CT findings can identify phenotypes with clinical and prognostic relevance in patients with EGPA. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 140 patients with EGPA and pulmonary involvement between 2014 and 2025. Chest CT findings were independently evaluated by two thoracic radiologists and analyzed using LCA to identify CT-based phenotypes. Reproducibility and clinical applicability were assessed by having radiologists reassign patients to phenotypes based on LCA-derived CT patterns while blinded to the original LCA assignments. Baseline characteristics and one-year clinical and radiological outcomes were compared across phenotypes. Modified Poisson regression was used to assess clinical relapse risk. RESULTS: LCA identified four distinct phenotypes: bronchial (32.1%; airway-predominant abnormalities), infiltrative (20.7%; parenchyma-predominant abnormalities), mixed (14.3%; combined bronchial and infiltrative features), and nonspecific (32.9%; without a dominant bronchial or infiltrative pattern). The bronchial and infiltrative phenotypes showed more favorable short-term outcomes, whereas the nonspecific phenotype mainly showed stable outcomes. The mixed phenotype remained associated with a higher risk of one-year clinical relapse after adjustment for age, sex, and baseline treatment. Radiologist reassignment showed excellent inter- and intra-observer agreement (Cohen's κ = 0.85 and 0.87). CONCLUSION: LCA enables the identification of CT-based phenotypes with distinct clinical characteristics and short-term outcome patterns in EGPA, suggesting potential prognostic value and a practical role in clinical management. KEY POINTS: QuestionCan latent class analysis (LCA) of chest CT findings identify imaging phenotypes of pulmonary involvement in eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA)? FindingsLCA identified four CT-based phenotypes (bronchial, infiltrative, mixed, and nonspecific), each characterized by distinct clinical and radiological features and short-term outcome patterns. Clinical relevanceCT-based phenotyping may help characterize pulmonary disease heterogeneity in EGPA and identify patients, particularly those with the mixed phenotype, who may require closer monitoring for clinical relapse.

articles.title: Progression After PRRT Is Not Just RECIST: Rethinking the Role of SSTR PET.
Low-Field MRI for Knee Imaging: Current Insights and Evidence From a Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Low-field magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has regained interest for musculoskeletal imaging due to advances in magnet design, hardware optimization, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based reconstruction, offering improved accessibility, patient comfort, and sustainability. PURPOSE: This systematic review aimed to explore and summarize the current status of low-field MRI for knee investigations. STUDY TYPE: Systematic review on MEDLINE, Cinhal, EMBASE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases. PROSPERO protocol (CRD42024544354). POPULATION: Approximately 3400 participants (8-89 years) encompassing healthy volunteers, community-based cohorts, and patients with diverse knee pathologies were evaluated. Few studies incorporate phantom experiments. FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: This review covered a range of very-low-field (< 0.1 T), conventional low-field (0.1-< 0.29 T), and upper-range low-field (> 0.3 T-0.55 T) with standard, extremity, open, and weight-bearing/standing systems. SE/FSE and GRE sequences, 3D GRE quantitative protocols, and AI-based were used. ASSESSMENT: Two reviewers independently extracted data on knee protocols, technical parameters, diagnostic performance, and reported advantages and limitations. STATISTICAL TESTS: Study quality was assessed using appropriate JBI critical appraisal tools. A narrative synthesis and descriptive analysis of the findings from the included studies are provided due to the heterogeneity of the intervention and outcome. RESULTS: From 3726 records, 31 were included. Low-field MRI demonstrated high diagnostic performance for meniscal and ligamentous injuries but lower sensitivity for early cartilage degeneration. Weight-bearing MRI provided distinct functional information but not direct equivalence to standard MRI. AI-enhanced reconstruction was evaluated in a limited number of single-center, vendor-specific studies and was associated with improved image quality and diagnostic confidence. Important limitations included lower signal-to-noise ratio, reduced spatial resolution, protocol heterogeneity, and limited pathology-validated evidence. DATA CONCLUSION: Low-field MRI may provide a clinically useful complementary option for selected knee meniscal and ligamentous indications. However, heterogeneous evidence, influenced by field strength, scanner design, sequences, and reference standards, limits claims of equivalence with high-field MRI, particularly for subtle cartilage lesions. Advances in hardware and AI have improved image quality and efficiency; however, evidence is limited and larger standardized multicenter studies are required. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 5. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 5.

articles.title: HARP: HARmonizing In-Vivo Single-Shell Diffusion MRI Using Phantom-Only Training.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Combining multi-site diffusion MRI (dMRI) data is hindered by inter-scanner variability, which confounds subsequent analysis. Previous harmonization methods require large, matched or traveling human subjects from multiple sites, which are impractical to acquire in many situations. This study aims to develop a deep learning-based dMRI harmonization framework that eliminates the reliance on multi-site in-vivo traveling human data for training. METHODS: HARP employs a voxel-wise 1D neural network trained on an easily transportable diffusion phantom. The model learns relationships between spherical harmonics coefficients of different sites without memorizing spatial structures. RESULTS: HARP reduced inter-scanner variability levels significantly in various measures. Quantitatively, it decreased inter-scanner variability as measured by standard error in FA (12%), MD (10%), and GFA (30%) with scan-rescan standard error as the baseline, while preserving fiber orientations and tractography after harmonization. CONCLUSION: We believe that HARP represents an important first step toward dMRI harmonization using only phantom data, thereby obviating the need for complex, matched in vivo multi-site cohorts. This phantom-only strategy substantially enhances the feasibility and scalability of quantitative dMRI for large-scale clinical studies.

articles.title: Investigation of gear design parameters for soft-gear-driven self-propelled colonoscopy robot.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Colonoscopy is the most effective method for colorectal cancer screening; however, successful insertion requires a high level of operator skill and may cause patient discomfort or injury. To address these challenges, self-propelled colonoscopy robots that generate propulsion at the distal tip have been actively investigated. In our previous work, we developed a self-propelled colonoscopy robot using a worm-gear mechanism; however, the use of rigid gears posed a potential risk of excessive contact force on the colonic wall. METHODS: In this study, we propose a self-propelled colonoscopy robot enabled by soft gears that combine compliant contact with gear-based power transmission. By reinterpreting the crawler-based propulsion concept as a soft spur gear driven by a worm-gear mechanism, the proposed design allows elastic deformation of the gear teeth under load, providing adaptive traction through compliant deformation of the gear teeth. Gear parameters were optimized using gear-design software, and four soft-gear configurations were fabricated to investigate their propulsion characteristics. RESULTS: The prototypes were fabricated using stereolithography 3D printing and evaluated using a colonoscopy training model. The robot achieved a maximum propulsive speed of 9.6 mm/s and a propulsive force of 1.5 N in straight sections. Gears with larger modules produced higher propulsion performance. In addition, the proposed coaxial double-worm-gear architecture enabled traversal of curved sections of the colon model under manual steering. CONCLUSION: These results demonstrate the mechanical feasibility of using soft gears as a propulsion mechanism for self-propelled colonoscopy robots. Although the evaluation was limited to a colonoscopy training model, the proposed design demonstrated stable propulsion in a colonoscopy training model while maintaining compliant contact with the intestinal wall. The simple and compact mechanical structure provides a promising proof of concept for future minimally invasive robotic endoscopy, although further ex vivo and in vivo validation will be required.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: Diagnostic Performance and Concordance of a BI-RADS-Output AI System in Mammography: A Retrospective Study of Radiologists-AI Collaboration.
articles.abstract: The identification of breast cancer using mammography and ultrasonography is influenced by inter-observer variability. Artificial intelligence (AI) models for breast classification have been investigated, but limited reports exist on Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS)-output AI systems. This study attempted to assess a BI-RADS-output AI system by comparing breast cancer detection rates among radiologist-only, AI-only, and combined interpretations, while also focusing on the AI's ability to identify cancers missed by radiologists and analyzing diagnostic concordance concerning imaging features and BI-RADS categories. A retrospective analysis was performed on 331 lesions from 321 consecutive breast cancer patients who underwent preoperative digital mammography and ultrasonography. McNemar's test was used to find the detection rates, and chi-square/Fisher's test, Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (ROC) analysis, and Kappa statistics were used to verify the diagnostic performance. The combined radiologist-AI interpretation achieved the highest cancer detection rate of 90.6%, which was higher than the radiologist's rate of 87.6% and the AI's rate of 84.0% (P < 0.05). The advantage was especially evident for BI-RADS 4B lesions, where AI alone decreased to 54.4%, while the combined method increased to 81.8%. AI found tumors that radiologists missed, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.840. There was a strong agreement for microcalcifications (κ = 0.827), but only a weak to moderate agreement for mass morphology and final BI-RADS classification (κ = 0.142-0.414). Although AI-radiologist agreement varied across different imaging features, their complementary strengths enabled improved cancer detection performance, supporting the role of BI-RADS-output AI systems as clinical decision-support tools rather than replacements for radiologists.

articles.title: Cardiac Image Segmentation Under Respiratory Motion Artifacts Using Different Modified U-Net Models.
articles.abstract: Precise segmentation of cardiac magnetic resonance images (CMR) is essential to quantitative measurements of the heart, yet it is often affected by respiratory motion misregistration's and this is particularly common in free-breathing patient environments. These artifacts reduce the quality of the image and present a big challenge to traditional deep learning models such as the baseline U-Net. This paper carries out a systematic evaluation of the capabilities of four alternate U-Net architectures, Attention U-Net, Dense U-Net, Residual U-Net and Sharp U-Net, on CMR data with synthetically added motion artifacts of various intensities. To add synthetic artifacts, the deformation fields were employed that mimic the realistic breathing-induced deformations and obtained the clean, mild, moderate, and severe moving conditions. Hybrid loss function that combines Dice, Focal, and Tversky losses was used to train each model to create robustness to class imbalance and boundary degradation. The segmentation quality was assessed by the following evaluation metrics: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff Distance (HD) and Jaccard Index (JI). Their results show that Sharp U-Net had the best overall performance with the highest average DSC (0.927) and lowest HD (3.62 mm) in severe motion conditions. The region centered attention mechanisms were also capable of withstanding these in Attention U-Net. The dense and Residual U-Nets did not perform much better than the baseline, and did not perform as well when there were severe artifacts. These results show the significance of architectural improvements and motion consciousness instruction strategies in guaranteeing the dependable segmentation. The article provides a scalable and reproducible methodology to assess the performance of motion-robust deep learning models for CMR and adaptable for use in other clinical diagnostic applications where respiratory gating is not available. The proposed framework provides a reproducible and computationally practical approach to motion-robust cardiac MRI segmentation. Sharp U-Net achieved the highest segmentation performance under severe respiratory motion, with a DSC of 0.784, compared with 0.778 for Attention U-Net, while requiring a slightly higher inference latency of approximately 28-30 ms per 256 × 256 slice and GPU memory consumption of approximately 1.8 GB. This modest computational overhead represents a trade-off between improved boundary preservation and computational efficiency and should be considered when deploying the model in resource-constrained clinical environments. Across the clean, mild, moderate, and severe respiratory motion conditions, Sharp U-Net achieved an average DSC of 0.927. Under the most challenging severe-motion condition, the DSC decreased to 0.784, while maintaining an ASSD of 1.69 mm, sensitivity of 0.823, precision of 0.774, and RVE of 8.9%.

articles.title: Radiomic Signatures of Smoking in Visually Normal Lung Parenchyma: Bilateral CT Analysis Using Machine Learning.
articles.abstract: Smoking is associated with structural and functional alterations in the lungs, some of which may be reflected in quantitative imaging features. Radiomics enables the extraction of high-dimensional image-derived descriptors and may provide information beyond routinely available clinical variables. We investigated whether bilateral lung radiomics, both independently and integrated with clinical variables, could classify patient-level smoking status. An exploratory secondary analysis was also performed to assess whether radiomic and clinical feature representations could discriminate smoking exposure intensity among smokers. A total of 506 patients were included, comprising 253 smokers and 253 nonsmokers. Right and left lung radiomic features were extracted separately from visually normal-appearing lung parenchyma on thoracic CT images. Multiple feature representations were evaluated, including right lung radiomics, left lung radiomics, concatenated right-left radiomics, summary/asymmetry radiomics, clinical variables alone, and radiomics combined with clinical variables. Clinical variables included age, sex, height, weight, and body mass index. Pack-years were excluded from the binary smoking status classification models to avoid target-related information leakage. For each binary classification task, a balanced internal hold-out set containing 25 smokers and 25 nonsmokers was reserved, while the remaining patients were evaluated using stratified tenfold cross-validation. Four feature selection or dimensionality reduction strategies and five classifier families were assessed, resulting in 435 model configurations across the main cohort and sex-specific subgroup analyses. Threshold selection was performed using the Youden index derived from cross-validated out-of-fold predictions. For the exploratory smoking exposure analysis, 253 smokers with available pack-year information were categorized into < 10, 10-20, and > 20 pack-year groups and evaluated using pooled stratified tenfold cross-validation. The best-performing radiomics-based configurations showed higher discrimination than the clinical-only configuration. The clinical-only random forest model achieved a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.673 and a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.610. Among radiomics-only configurations, concatenated bilateral radiomics achieved a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.734 and a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.712. The strongest hold-out discrimination was obtained using concatenated bilateral radiomics combined with clinical variables, ReliefF feature selection, and stacking classification, achieving a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.803, balanced accuracy of 0.700, sensitivity of 0.720, and specificity of 0.680. Feature selection stability analysis showed that the final concatenated bilateral radiomics + clinical configuration retained five clinical variables and 15 radiomic features, several of which were repeatedly selected across cross-validation folds. Sex-specific subgroup analyses showed moderate but variable performance. In the exploratory three-class smoking exposure analysis, integrating left lung radiomics with clinical variables yielded the most balanced class-wise performance, achieving the highest balanced accuracy (0.658) and the highest sensitivity for the intermediate 10-20 pack-year group (0.417), although the clinical-only model achieved the highest macro-AUC. Bilateral lung radiomics showed potential for patient-level smoking status classification, particularly when combined with clinical variables. These findings suggest that quantitative imaging features could provide complementary information beyond routinely available patient-level variables. The exploratory smoking exposure analysis further suggested that radiomics + clinical configurations may contain limited information related to smoking exposure intensity, although intermediate exposure remained challenging to discriminate. However, the moderate performance, subgroup variability, and lack of external validation indicate that this approach should be considered investigational until confirmed in larger independent cohorts.

articles.title: Incremental Prognostic Value of White Matter Hyperintensity Beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System for Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the additional prognostic value of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease (CAD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 1085 patients who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography and brain magnetic resonance imaging between November 2018 and December 2022. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate the predictive values, and the C-statistic was employed to determine their discriminatory power. RESULTS: 170 (15.7%) patients experienced MACE during a median follow-up of 63.1 months. WMH remained a significant and independent risk factor for predicting MACE after adjustments with clinical variables alone or with CAD-RADS. In the training set, the clinical-CAD-RADS-WMH model showed area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.719, 0.740, and 0.776 for predicting MACE at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. The model showed a consistent performance trend with AUCs of 0.819, 0.836, and 0.823 in the test set over 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. Both the addition of WMH to the clinical model and to the clinical plus CAD-RADS model significantly increased the C-statistic index (p = 0.007, p = 0.038 in the training set and p = 0.002, p = 0.004 in the test set). These trends continued to be present when WMH was analyzed as a continuous variable. CONCLUSION: An elevated WMH was related to a higher risk of MACE in patients with suspected or established CAD. Moreover, WMH demonstrated additional prognostic value for MACE beyond CAD-RADS.

articles.title: Peritumoral Edema Outperforms Solid Tumor for Predicting TERTp Mutation in IDH Wild-Type Gliomas: A Multiparametric Diffusion MRI Histogram Study with Prognostic Analysis.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To investigate the preoperative predictive value of histogram features of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) parameters for isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) and telomerase reverse transcriptase promoter (TERTp) mutation status in adult diffuse gliomas, and to identify independent prognostic factors for overall survival (OS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 404 patients who underwent DWI, DKI, and IVIM imaging. Region-specific logistic regression models were developed using stratified 70:30 training and hold-out test splits. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curves were used to assess predictive performance. Decision-curve, synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) sensitivity, and bootstrap stability analyses were also performed. Prognostic factors were evaluated using Cox regression in 343 patients with follow-up. RESULTS: For IDH prediction, areas under the curve (AUCs) ranged from 0.874 to 0.920 in solid tumor and 0.902 to 0.936 in peritumoral edema, without significant between-region differences. For TERTp prediction in IDH wild-type gliomas, peritumoral edema models achieved higher AUCs than their solid tumor counterparts: DWI, 0.893 versus 0.677 (P = 0.019); DKI, 0.916 versus 0.754 (P = 0.036); IVIM, 0.934 versus 0.819 (P = 0.022); and combined, 0.948 versus 0.819 (P = 0.020). Decision-curve analysis favored the peritumoral edema combined model, and the regional discrimination pattern persisted after SMOTE balancing. In the overall cohort, peritumoral edema Kskewness, D*10th, and fentropy were independently associated with OS, alongside age, IDH status, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter methylation, and Ki-67 LI. Within the IDH wild-type subgroup, age, TERTp status, and Ki-67 LI were independent prognostic factors. CONCLUSION: Diffusion histogram models provided high discrimination for IDH status in both regions. Peritumoral edema models offered superior TERTp prediction in IDH wild-type gliomas, while selected peritumoral features provided prognostic information in the overall cohort.

articles.title: CT-based Multimodal Model for Early Severity Prediction in Hyperlipidemic Acute Pancreatitis: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a multimodal model integrating pancreatic parenchymal and peripancreatic fat radiomics with independent clinical predictors for early severity stratification in hyperlipidemic acute pancreatitis (HLAP). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 356 patients with HLAP from three centers. HLAP was defined as acute pancreatitis (AP) with serum triglycerides ≥11.3 mmol/L or 5.65 to 11.3 mmol/L, accompanied by lactescent serum after exclusion of other etiologies. Patients from Center 1 were assigned to the training (n = 193) and internal validation (n = 83) cohorts, whereas patients from Centers 2 and 3 formed the external test cohort (n = 80). One noncontrast abdominal computed tomography examination acquired within 72 hours of symptom onset was analyzed per patient. Clinical, radiomics, and fusion models were developed using four machine-learning algorithms. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and DeLong tests. RESULTS: The cohort included 107 patients with severe AP and 249 with nonsevere AP. The median age was 37.0 years (interquartile range, 31.75-45.0), and 268 patients (75.3%) were male. The final pancreatic parenchyma-peripancreatic fat-clinical combined model achieved AUCs of 0.947 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.897-0.986) and 0.846 (95% CI, 0.735-0.940) in the internal validation and external test cohorts, respectively, with external sensitivity and specificity of 0.611 and 0.871. DeLong testing showed significant improvements over the pancreatic parenchyma radiomics, 15 mm peripancreatic fat radiomics, and clinical models in internal validation (all p < 0.05), but not in external testing (all p > 0.05). CONCLUSION: The proposed multimodal model showed good discrimination and interpretability for early HLAP severity stratification and may support individualized clinical decision-making.

articles.title: The distinctive body habitus of frontotemporal dementia sagging brain syndrome.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Frontotemporal dementia sagging-brain-syndrome (FTDSBS) is characterized radiographically by severe brain sagging. However, an underlying CSF leak can be found in only a minority of patients. Clinical observation suggests that some of these patients have a distinctive body habitus consisting of tall stature and obesity. The purpose of the present study was to evaluate FTDSBS patients for the presence of this particular body habitus. METHODS: This single center cross-sectional study included a consecutive group of FTDSBS patients, with or without an underlying spinal CSF-venous fistula. Comparison groups included patients with CSF-venous fistulas without FTDSBS and U.S. population reference estimates from NHANES. RESULTS: The mean age of the 43 men and five women with FTDSBS was 52.8 years. Patients with FTDSBS were taller and more obese than patients with CSF-venous fistulas without FTDSBS and the general population. The differences in height (5.5 to 7.3 cm [2.2 to 2.9 inches]), weight (15 to 27.7 kg [33 to 61 lbs]), and BMI (1.9 to 6.8 kg/m2) were statistically significant (p<0.001). These differences were especially pronounced for patients with FTDSBS who did not have an identifiable underlying spinal CSF leak. DISCUSSION: A distinctive body habitus consisting of tall stature and obesity is common among patients with FTDSBS especially among those who do not have an identifiable underlying spinal CSF leak. This may help generate hypotheses regarding the pathophysiology and eventual treatment of this devastating disorder.

articles.title: Salvage CT Myelography: Same-Session Repositioning to Localize Spinal CSF Leaks.
articles.abstract: Localization of spinal CSF leaks may require multiple myelograms when the initially suspected CSF leak type is not identified. We describe a salvage CT myelography (CTM) technique in which the patient is repositioned during the same myelographic session to evaluate for an alternative CSF leak type. Eleven patients underwent salvage CTM at three institutions. When the initially suspected CSF leak was not identified, the patient was repositioned with the lumbar puncture needle remaining in place, and additional small contrast boluses and targeted CT acquisitions were performed. Salvage CTM identified alternative CSF leak types across several diagnostic scenarios involving ventral, lateral, dorsal/dorsolateral, and sacral dural tears and CSF-venous fistulas. The mean procedural time was 55.9 minutes, mean contrast dose was 12.5 cc, and mean dose-length product was 2180 mGy-cm. Salvage CTM is an adaptive, same-session strategy that may reduce the need for repeat myelographic sessions and additional lumbar punctures while maintaining reasonable procedural times and contrast doses.

articles.title: Early Acquisition Timing and CSF Venous Fistula Conspicuity on Lateral Decubitus CT Myelography.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The optimal acquisition timing of lateral decubitus CT myelography (LD-CTM) for visualizing CSF venous fistulas (CVFs) remains uncertain. We compared known-site CVF conspicuity on acquisitions initiated 1 and 2 minutes after the start of intrathecal contrast injection to determine whether timing affected fistula visibility. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective paired-image study included 35 patients with LD-CTM findings classified as high-probability or definite CVF according to the Duke CSF-Venous Fistula Confidence Score. Paired axial image sets spanning the depicted fistula were selected from the two acquisitions at matched anatomic levels. Three neurointerventional radiologists, blinded to acquisition timing and clinical information, independently assigned a visibility score to each acquisition-specific image set, ranging from 0 (not visible) to 3 (clearly visible). Scores of 2 or 3 met the prespecified threshold for visibility. Reviewers also selected which image set better depicted the fistula. The primary outcome was the difference in patient-level median visibility scores between acquisitions. Rating-level threshold visibility was analyzed using mixed-effects logistic regression, with an exploratory model additionally including measured intrathecal attenuation. RESULTS: The patient-level median visibility score was higher on the 1-minute than on the 2-minute phases (3 [IQR, 2-3] versus 1 [IQR, 0-2]; P < .001). At the reviewer level, threshold visibility was achieved in 92/105 ratings (87.6%) at 1 minute compared with 48/105 ratings (45.7%) at 2 minutes. The odds of threshold visibility were higher at 1 minute (OR, 9.73; 95% CI, 4.70 to 20.15; P < .001). After inclusion of measured fistula-level intrathecal attenuation, a residual phase association remained (attenuation-adjusted OR, 5.02; 95% CI, 2.25 to 11.19; P < .001). The 1-minute acquisition was preferred in 26/35 patients (74.3%), the 2-minute acquisition in 5/35 (14.3%), and the phases were rated equal in 4/35 (11.4%). CONCLUSIONS: Under this standardized fixed-delay protocol, the 1-minute acquisition provided greater known-site CVF conspicuity overall, while the 2-minute acquisition provided complementary information in a minority of patients. These findings support multiphasic imaging but do not establish a universally optimal acquisition time.

articles.title: Federated Learning-Based Multi-Task Framework for Privacy-Preserving Diagnosis of Muscle Invasion in Bladder Cancer.
articles.abstract: Accurate diagnosis of muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) is critical for effective treatment planning, yet remains challenging owing to the scarcity of large-scale multicenter datasets and stringent data privacy requirements. To address these issues, we propose a federated learning (FL)-based framework for privacy-preserving MIBC diagnosis. The framework enables multi-institutional collaboration by training local models on site-specific data and aggregating them into a global model through secure parameter exchange, without transferring raw data. Furthermore, we introduce a multi-task learning architecture that simultaneously performs tumor segmentation and invasion classification, supported by a split-attention convolutional module designed to improve feature discrimination. Experimental results on MRI datasets from four medical centers show that our proposed multi‑task federated learning framework yields an AUC of 0.844, outperforming both single‑center models and the single‑task federated baseline (AUC = 0.829), and exhibits robustness under heterogeneous data distributions. Ablation experiments showed that incorporating the split-attention convolutional module increased the AUC of the multi-task FL model from 0.818 to 0.844.

articles.title: Application and Improvement of YOLO11 for Carotid Plaque Detection in Handheld Ultrasound Images.
articles.abstract: Early and accurate detection of carotid plaques is clinically significant for stroke risk assessment and primary care screening. To address challenges such as low resolution, small target size, and blurred boundaries in handheld ultrasound images of carotid plaques, this paper proposes an improved YOLO11n model named YOLO11-MGD. The model introduces the C2PSA_Mona module to suppress interference from normal anatomical structures and incorporates the C3k2_GCConv module to enhance global context modeling capabilities, thereby alleviating semantic fragmentation caused by heterogeneous plaques. Additionally, it integrates a Dynamic Head to achieve joint dynamic attention allocation across scale, space, and task dimensions, and it designs the Inner_MPDIoU loss function to improve bounding box regression accuracy for irregular plaques.
