Experimental results show that on a self-constructed dataset containing 2078 carotid plaque images, YOLO11-MGD achieves a mean mAP50 of 93.16%, outperforming several mainstream object detection models. While maintaining its lightweight advantage, the proposed method significantly enhances the accuracy and robustness of carotid plaque detection in low-quality ultrasound images and demonstrates good application value for primary care stroke risk screening.

articles.title: Field-Strength Dependence of Automated Subcortical Volumetry: A Paired 3 T-7 T Benchmarking Study of BrainSuite, FastSurfer and NextBrain.
articles.abstract: Automated segmentation pipelines are widely used for quantitative assessment of subcortical brain structures, yet it remains unclear whether measurements obtained at different magnetic field strengths are numerically interchangeable. This study evaluated the cross-field agreement and inter-software consistency of automated subcortical volumetry using paired 3T and 7T structural MRI data from 30 healthy adults. T1-weighted images were independently processed using BrainSuite, FastSurfer and NextBrain. Volumes of the bilateral putamen, globus pallidus, nucleus accumbens, thalamus and caudate nucleus were analysed. Within-software agreement between 3 and 7T measurements was assessed using two-way mixed-effects, single-measure intraclass correlation coefficients for absolute agreement. Inter-software agreement was examined separately at 3T and 7T using both absolute agreement and consistency intraclass correlation coefficients. All within-software regional comparisons and selected inter-software comparisons were further evaluated using Bland-Altman analyses. Cross-field agreement varied markedly across software packages and anatomical regions. BrainSuite showed poor absolute agreement across all regions, whereas FastSurfer and NextBrain demonstrated moderate-to-good agreement in selected structures. Inter-software consistency was generally higher than absolute agreement, indicating preservation of relative participant ranking despite systematic differences in measured volumes. Segmentation failures were more frequent at 7T, particularly for BrainSuite. Bland-Altman analyses confirmed software- and region-specific systematic differences and wide limits of agreement. These findings indicate that the evaluated automated segmentation pipelines do not provide field-strength-invariant subcortical volume estimates. Measurements obtained at 3T and 7T, or using different software packages, should not be considered directly interchangeable without pipeline-specific validation or harmonisation.

articles.title: Generative AI-Based Data Augmentation for Oral Lesion Classification: The PhotoMOCI Dataset and Benchmark.
articles.abstract: Early detection of oral cancer via photographic imaging presents a promising avenue for large-scale oral cavity screening. However, the development of robust deep learning models is frequently hampered by the scarcity of high-quality, annotated datasets. To address this limitation, a novel and well-curated resource, the Photographic Multi-purpose Oral Cancer Imaging (PhotoMOCI) dataset, is introduced for developing models across multiple diagnostic tasks in oral oncology. Then, a comprehensive benchmark study was conducted to investigate how various data augmentation strategies influence the performance of image classifiers. Our analysis spans different generative AI frameworks, evaluating the efficacy of traditional methods against advanced generative approaches, including generative adversarial networks (GANs) and diffusion models (DMs). Additionally, we propose the Synthetic Image Filter (SIF), a mechanism to select specific samples based on two auxiliary models: Synthetic Proxy Classifier to ensure samples are representative of the target class and Synthetic Image Detector to verify they appear realistic, thereby selecting only the high-utility images that contribute to improving downstream performance. Across the evaluated datasets and classifiers, the best SIF-filtered setup improves accuracy over traditional augmentation in all cases, with gains of +1.73% and +2.35% on PhotoMOCI and +2.38% and +2.08% on KOCD for ResNet50 and ViT, respectively. Our findings reveal that while the direct application of generative data augmentation may yield performance drops, the integration of SIF, considering (i) how synthetic data looks real and (ii) how it reflects the discriminative features of the belonging class, provides a simple yet effective mechanism to filter out synthetic samples that confuse the classifier during training.

articles.title: Performance of Naïve Spectral Geometric Models in Histopathology AI.
articles.abstract: Spectral geometric methods provide mathematically interpretable representations of tissue morphology, yet their standalone performance in histopathology artificial intelligence has not been systematically evaluated. This study benchmarks purely spectral pipelines across representative digital pathology and spatial omics tasks relative to convolutional baselines. Spectral features derived from graph Laplacians, heat kernel signatures, spectral wavelet energy, Slepian concentrations, fractal descriptors, and persistent homology were extracted from histopathology patches using fixed-grid graphs. Features were processed using spectral neural operators and gradient boosting. Four tasks were evaluated: binary breast cancer classification (BreaKHis), multi-class glioblastoma region-patch classification, spatial transcriptomics prediction (10× Visium), and spot-wise denoising. Cross-validation and leave-one-slide-out strategies were applied. Metrics included accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), mean squared error, and Pearson correlation. Equivalence between spectral and CNN models was not established within the prespecified ±0.03 AUC margin. Purely spectral models achieved lower performance than convolutional baselines, with AUC differences of 0.12-0.23. The CNN→LGBM model achieved an accuracy of 0.83 ± 0.06, balanced accuracy of 0.73 ± 0.10, and AUC of 0.80 ± 0.13. Equivalence was not established within the prespecified margin. Fusion achieved balanced accuracy of 0.73 ± 0.08, equal to the CNN baseline mean balanced accuracy, without surpassing CNN AUC. Spatial transcriptomics prediction showed limited cross-slide generalization (Pearson correlation 0.06), whereas spot-wise denoising under sparse conditions showed competitive performance. Spectral geometric models do not outperform convolutional methods for classification or segmentation but provide complementary utility in denoising and sparse spatial settings.

articles.title: TriKey AutoRefine: A Stability-Aware Framework Built on Pan-organ Segmentation Radiomics for Chronic Kidney Disease Staging.
articles.abstract: Accurate and generalizable imaging‑based staging of chronic kidney disease remains challenging due to segmentation variability, feature instability, and heterogeneous clinical presentations. To address these gaps, a clinically aligned pan‑organ radiomics workflow for multi‑class chronic kidney disease staging was proposed. A total of 587 subjects from 3 centers were included, with chest and abdominal computed tomography scans paired with clinical and body-composition measurements. Segmentation‑induced variability was quantified within the pan‑organ segmentation system, revealing systematic anatomical and feature‑level patterns that enabled the construction of a robust and generalizable feature foundation. Building on these observations, the TriKey autorefine framework was introduced as a structured refinement strategy incorporating Shapley additive explanations guided refinement, clinically informed class weighting, and automatic parameter optimization. Using this framework, strong performance was achieved across chronic kidney disease staging tasks. In the standard 5‑class setting, high discriminative ability was obtained: training macro area under the curve 0.925 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.923-0.927); validation macro area under the curve 0.875 ± 0.0087 (95% CI 0.858-0.892). In the clinically actionable 4‑class grouping, even stronger performance was observed, with a mean macro area under the curve of 0.915 ± 0.0060 (95% CI 0.903-0.927). Interpretability was further supported through radiomics-clinical correlation analyses, which confirmed that the selected pan organ features correspond to measurable physiological variations associated with chronic kidney disease progression. This study demonstrates a robust, interpretable, and clinically grounded pan‑organ radiomics pipeline for chronic kidney disease staging, providing a generalizable foundation for future pan-organ radiomics research in nephrology and broader clinical imaging applications.

articles.title: Deep Learning Super-Resolution CT Versus Ultra-High-Resolution CT: A Direct Comparison in Cadaveric Human Lungs.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Deep learning-based high-resolution computed tomography (CT) of the lung parenchyma has not been directly compared with ultra-high-resolution CT (UHR-CT). We compared image quality between deep learning-based super-resolution CT and UHR-CT using identical cadaveric human lungs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 10 cadaveric human lungs scanned using conventional CT and UHR-CT at two dose levels (9 mGy, 2 mGy). Five reconstruction methods were evaluated, including deep learning-based synthetic super-resolution CT (CCT-1024-PIQE) and UHR-CT-derived high-resolution images reconstructed using a deep learning-based denoising algorithm (UHR-1024-AiCE). Two radiologists independently assessed the bronchioles, seven abnormal findings, and overall image quality using a 5-point scale. The objective image noise was also quantified. Statistical comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. RESULTS: At 9 mGy, no significant differences were observed in the bronchioles, whereas UHR-1024-AiCE demonstrated higher scores than CCT-1024-PIQE for ground-glass opacities and intralobular reticulation (all P ≤ 0.007). At 2 mGy, CCT-1024-PIQE showed no significant differences from UHR-1024-AiCE for most findings. Compared with the 512-matrix reconstructions, CCT-1024-PIQE achieved consistently higher visual scores at both dose levels (most comparisons, P < 0.05). Image noise increased at 2 mGy across all methods, while PIQE-based reconstructions showed lower noise (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Deep learning-based super-resolution CT showed no significant differences from UHR-CT in many pulmonary findings, particularly under low-dose conditions, while improving visualization compared to conventional 512-matrix reconstructions.

articles.title: Feasibility, Safety, and Effectiveness of Bleomycin Electrosclerotherapy in Patients with "Giant Hepatic Hemangiomas".
articles.abstract: This retrospective study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and effectiveness of bleomycin electrosclerotherapy (BEST) in nine patients with symptomatic, size-progressive "giant hepatic hemangiomas" unsuitable for surgery. BEST was performed under general anesthesia using six CT-guided needle electrodes. Bleomycin was administered intravenously in three patients and intralesionally in six (3,000-16,430 IU). Follow-up MRI was recommended three months after treatment. Median volume reduction at first follow-up was 18.3% (IQR, 2.7%-36.2%; P = .020) at a median of 77 days (IQR, 44-117 days). Extended follow-up in eight patients demonstrated a median volume reduction of 47.0% (IQR, 17.5%-73.2%; P = .016) at 299 days (IQR, 256-739 days). Six of nine patients reported symptom improvement during follow-up. No major complications occurred; adverse events included three asymptomatic perihepatic hematomas and one intercostal neuralgia requiring prolonged analgesic treatment. BEST was feasible and associated with lesion volume reduction and symptom improvement in this cohort. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Case Series.

articles.title: Digital Twin Control Framework Uncovers Individualized Cross-Scale Links Between Functional Connectivity Deviations, Communication Impairment, and Molecular Mechanisms in Autism.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is hallmarked by pronounced inter-individual heterogeneity in brain function and clinical manifestations. Conventional neuroimaging studies yield highly inconsistent findings, as extrinsic confounding factors and intrinsic disease heterogeneity mask ASD-specific functional connectivity (FC) signatures, hampering the identification of individualized neural mechanisms linked to symptom severity. METHODS: We developed a digital twin control analytical framework based on deep contrastive learning. By comparing each ASD participant with their matched digital twin control, we quantified individual-specific FC deviations. Principal component analysis was applied to extract the core aberrant pattern, followed by multi-dimensional analyses and validation including clinical correlation, transcriptomic decoding, neurotransmitter and mitochondrial co-localization, as well as disease and cognitive enrichment. RESULTS: The model effectively disentangled disease‑related from non‑disease‑related variations. The identified dominant aberrant FC pattern was significantly associated with Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS) communication scores, suggesting its associated with to communication impairment. This pattern showed convergent associations with synaptic pathways, excitatory/inhibitory neuronal signatures, critical developmental windows and subcortical structures, and exhibited negative spatial association with multiple neurotransmitter systems and mitochondrial respiratory complexes. Biological validation further supported its ASD specificity and communication‑related cognitive relevance. CONCLUSIONS: Leveraging the twin control analytical framework, this study provides an exploratory cross-scale framework linking individualized FC deviations with clinical, transcriptomic, neurochemical, and mitochondrial maps. The findings indicate that communication difficulties in ASD may partly arise from multi-scale disturbances in neural integration, social-perceptual processing and activity-dependent cellular energy regulation.

articles.title: Decoding individual differences in mental information from human brain responses predicted by deep neural networks.
articles.abstract: Brain decoding using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has high potential for evaluating unobservable mental information that varies across individuals in everyday situations. Although estimating individual differences in mental information using brain decoding could be effective for social applications, especially in neuromarketing, the physical constraints and high costs of fMRI limit the practical application in real-world settings. To overcome these limitations, we propose a framework to estimate individual differences in decodable mental information using brain responses predicted by deep neural networks (DNNs). In this framework, DNN-based models are trained to predict fMRI responses to natural movie scenes. Then, additional fMRI measurements are no longer required because mental information for new movie scenes can be decoded from the predicted responses instead of the measured ones. A large-scale analysis revealed that the proposed predicted-response decoding captures individual difference patterns consistent with those derived from conventional measured-response decoding across various cognitive domains. Of the 88 cognitive labels associated with movie scenes, individual difference patterns could be captured for more than 70% of the labels. This framework offers a promising approach for evaluating personal mental information with substantially reduced reliance on fMRI, thereby expanding the potential for social applications of brain decoding.

articles.title: Do neuroimaging data have higher-order interactions?
articles.abstract: Recent advances in the physics of complex systems have motivated the study of higher-order structure in neuroimaging data, including functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), and magnetoencephalography (MEG). Despite the proliferation of proposed measures, the meaning of "higher-order" is often left implicit, and the term is used inconsistently across studies. In this work, we clarify the distinction between higher-order interactions and higher-order dependencies. Higher-order interactions necessarily imply higher-order dependencies, but the converse does not hold: systems can exhibit higher-order dependencies in the absence of higher-order interactions, as in the case of Gaussian variables. We present several equivalent definitions of higher-order interactions for continuous data, illustrate them using simple model systems, and use them to assess the specificity of measures commonly applied in neuroimaging. We show that these measures are not specific to higher-order interactions. Consequently, although existing studies support the presence of higher-order dependencies in neuroimaging data, they do not provide conclusive evidence for the presence of higher-order interactions.

articles.title: Coarse motor-state structure across paired preoperative fMRI and intraoperative ECoG in patients with brain tumors.
articles.abstract: Presurgical motor mapping in patients with tumors near eloquent motor cortex is commonly based on task-evoked activation maps, yet local BOLD responses may be difficult to interpret in lesion-affected tissue because of anatomical distortion, altered vascular coupling, and variability in task performance. In this study, we used a four-state motor paradigm spanning Action, kinesthetic motor imagery (IMG), Watch, and recent-action recall (REC) - to test whether coarse task-state relationships are preserved across paired preoperative fMRI and intraoperative ECoG in10 patients with brain tumors. Activation summaries and preoperative task familiarization were used to support task engagement, representational similarity analysis (RSA) was used to characterize within-modality state geometry, and cross-modal RSA was used to assess shared organization. Across modalities, Action and IMG showed relatively similar response patterns, Watch was more distinct, and REC occupied an intermediate position that should be interpreted cautiously because of the fixed task order. Cross-modal RSA showed positive correspondence between fMRI and ECoG representational dissimilarity matrices, supporting a shared coarse state structure rather than fine-grained equivalence between modalities. These findings support a hypothesis-generating, relation-based complementary framework for interpreting functional organization in patients with brain tumors, while the limited state space, clinically determined ECoG coverage, fixed task order, and indirect verification of internally generated states warrant cautious interpretation.

articles.title: The Visual Cortex and Beyond: Investigating Long-Term Cortical Plasticity Following Monocular Deprivation.
articles.abstract: AIM: To characterise short- and long-term plastic changes in cortical and subcortical structures induced by ultra-long (five-day) monocular deprivation (MD), and to assess the extent and regional specificity of structural changes and their reversibility following the restoration of binocular vision. METHODS: In this single-arm longitudinal study, 21 healthy adults underwent five structural MRI sessions: at baseline, during MD on days 1, 3 and 5, and after a seven-day recovery period (day 12). MD was induced by occluding the right eye with a translucent eye patch for five consecutive days. Grey matter volume (GMV) changes were analysed using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) for whole-brain effects and generalised estimating equations (GEE) to model temporal trajectories in predefined cortical and subcortical regions. RESULTS: Ultra-long MD induced dynamic GMV changes in primary and higher visual cortices, with exploratory changes also in subcortical and cerebellar structures. VBM showed cumulative volume increases in bilateral occipital cortex, including calcarine, lateral occipital and fusiform regions, and adjacent cerebellar lobules, peaking between days 3 and 5. Region-wise modelling resolved the temporal build-up of these changes across visual, subcortical and sensorimotor regions; after correction for multiple comparisons, a time-dependent effect remained in occipital and ventral occipito-temporal cortex (occipital pole, fusiform and calcarine cortex), converging with the voxel-wise result. Following binocular restoration, an exploratory GMV decrease was observed selectively in the left middle occipital gyrus, while an exploratory increase was observed in the left hippocampus, compatible with persistent plasticity in associative memory networks. CONCLUSION: Prolonged sensory imbalance via ultra-long MD induces rapid, region-specific and possibly persistent GMV plasticity in the adult brain. These changes follow temporally stratified trajectories across visual, subcortical and integrative systems, consistent with models of homeostatic and hierarchical plasticity. Corrected evidence supports cumulative occipital plasticity during deprivation; whether the exploratory extra-visual and post-recovery changes reflect persistent adaptation requires confirmation. MD-based paradigms thus offer a controlled window on structural plasticity in both healthy individuals and clinical populations.

articles.title: Feasibility of canine minibeam radiotherapy (MBRT) with a dual-robot kilovoltage x-ray system.
articles.abstract: To evaluate the feasibility of delivering minibeam radiotherapy (MBRT) to a canine glioblastoma patient using a novel low-cost dual-robot kilovoltage (kV) x-ray system.  Approach: A workflow to perform MBRT using a tungsten collimator with 300 μm slits was developed for the 225 kVp x-ray source system. A Monte Carlo (MC) model of MBRT was built in TOPAS and validated with EBT4 measurements in-air and in a solid water phantom. A non-coplanar MBRT treatment plan with 2 mm Al- and 0.5 mm Cu-filtered beams was created for the canine patient and compared to a clinical 6 MV VMAT plan. A full set and individual minibeam fields were delivered to a canine head phantom with an intracranial film to verify plan feasibility.Main results: Measured and MC-simulated peak-to-valley dose ratios in-air and in the water phantom agreed within ≤ 2σ. Open-beam and collimated peak dose measurements at depths acquired with films in the water phantom agreed with simulations with mean relative differences of 1% and 2%, respectively. MBRT treatment plan spatial fractionation was preserved in healthy tissue for tissue-sparing benefits. Mean MBRT doses to organs at risk were within 15% of VMAT, except for skin (+52% for Al- and +48% for Cu-filtered beams), bone (+28% for Al and +22% for Cu) and the right ear (-39% for Al and -42% for Cu). Dose difference map average in the canine head phantom was 2.3 ± 1.2% for one and 3.5 ± 2.2% for two minibeam fields. Significance: These results demonstrate the feasibility of MBRT delivery using the novel x-ray system to a canine due to spatial fractionation and adequate depth dose delivered to the tumor.

articles.title: Azygos Venous Pressure and Respiratory Modulation of CSF-Venous Pressure Gradients in SIH and IIH patients.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The azygos system is a major drainage pathway of the thoracic spinal venous network and may participate in the regulation of spinal CSF resorption. CSF-pressure disorders such as spontaneous intracranial hypotension (SIH) related to a CSF-venous fistula (CSFVF) and idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) could therefore be influenced by the hemodynamics and the pressure of this system. However, azygos pressure and its respiratory modulation remain poorly characterized. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 54 consecutive patients who underwent combined venous and CSF pressure measurements between September 2025 and February 2026. Forty-five patients were investigated for SIH/CSFVF and 9 for IIH. Pressures were recorded in the azygos system, intracranial venous sinuses, right atrium (CVP), and lumbar CSF compartment. Dynamic measurements were obtained during resisted inspiration, breath holding, and Valsalva. Values are reported as mean ± SD or median [IQR], as appropriate. Paired respiratory changes were assessed with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: Overall, median azygos pressure was 8.0 [6.0-9.8] mm Hg and was modestly but significantly higher than CVP: 6.5 [4.0-8.0] mm Hg; median paired difference, +2.0 [1.0-3.0] mm Hg; p < .001. Azygos pressure did not differ significantly between SIH/CSFVF and IIH groups: 8.0 [6.0-9.0] versus 9.0 [8.0-10.0] mm Hg; p = .34. Level-by-level measurements in 25 patients showed only limited cranial pressure decline, with median pressure of 8.0 [6.0-9.0] mm Hg in the caudal L2-T10 segment and 7.0 [5.0-8.0] mm Hg in the cranial T9-T5 segment; p = .007. Resisted inspiration produced the largest CSF-azygos gradient, increasing from 0.0 [-3.0 to 5.0] to 12.0 [11.0-15.0] mm Hg, primarily because azygos pressure decreased from 7.0 to -6.0 mm Hg while CSF pressure remained stable. CONCLUSIONS: In the investigated population, median azygos pressure was 8mmHg, close to CVP, and stable along the spinal axis. Resisted inspiration markedly increased the CSF-azygos gradient by lowering azygos pressure, providing a hemodynamic explanation for improved CSF-venous fistula conspicuity during resisted-inspiration myelography.

articles.title: Image Quality of Non-Contrast Neurological Images on Energy-Integrating versus Silicon Photon-Counting Detector CT.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this work was to evaluate image quality of non-contrast neurological CT scans on a commercially available energy-integrating detector (EID) CT compared to a prototype deep silicon (dSi) photon-counting detector CT (PCCT). A cohort of subjects scanned on the EID-CT (Apex CT, GE HealthCare, Waukesha, WI) was retrospectively recruited. A second cohort of prospectively recruited subjects was scanned on the prototype dSi-PCCT CT using deep learning (DL) recon. Image quality was assessed by four neuroradiologists on a 5-point Likert scale for sharpness, noise, and presence of artifacts, differentiation of gray-white matter, and structural confidence in the lentiform nucleus and insular ribbon. Reader agreement was assessed through a linearly weighted Cohen's kappa. Contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) between gray and white matter was determined. Differences between the median Likert scores and CNRs of the two cohorts were assessed with the Mann-Whitney U test. Reader agreement was fair on average ([Formula: see text]). Median Likert scores of the dSi-PCCT with DL recon cohort were statistically superior compared to the median scores of the EID-CT scores for sharpness, noise, gray-white matter differentiation, and structural confidence of the lentiform nucleus and insular ribbon. No statistical difference was detected in the presence of artifacts between the cohorts. Average CNRs were 1.45±0.14 and 1.53±0.08 for the EID-CT and dSi-PCCT cohorts, respectively, but no significant difference was detected (p = 0.72). Increased sharpness, lower noise, and better ability to differentiate structures demonstrate improved image quality and the potential for utilizing PCCT in non-contrast neurological imaging tasks.

articles.title: From contouring variability to dosimetric impact: a comprehensive assessment of online adaptive MR-guided SBRT for pancreatic cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify inter-physician contouring variability and evaluate its dosimetric impact in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients treated with daily online adaptive MR-guided stereotactic body radiotherapy (MRgSBRT), to assess safety and clinical robustness of online contouring. METHODS: Fifty treatment sessions from ten PDAC patients treated with 50 Gy in five fractions on a 1.5 T MR-Linac were retrospectively analyzed. During each treatment session ("online"), targets and organs-at-risk (OARs) within 3 cm of the tumor were delineated by seven physicians working on the MR-Linac. All structures were re-contoured offline by a single pancreatic-expert radiation oncologist ("reference"). Geometric agreement was assessed using Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), Mean Distance to Agreement (MDA), and 95 % Hausdorff Distance (HD95). Dosimetric analyses were performed on delivered treatment plans using both online and reference contours, with evaluation based on fraction-wise worst-case dose metrics. RESULTS: High geometric concordance was observed for stomach and duodenum, whereas smaller or anatomically complex structures (GTV, major vessels, bile duct) showed greater variability. Online GTVs were larger than reference contours. Despite these differences, target coverage (V50Gy and V35Gy) was maintained with online contours. While occasional per-fraction gastrointestinal (GI) dose constraint exceedances were identified using reference contours, fraction-wise worst-case analysis showed GI doses remained within clinical tolerance for nearly all patients. CONCLUSION: Daily online adaptive MRgSBRT for PDAC provides robust target coverage and clinically acceptable OAR sparing, despite contouring variability. Multi-physician online contouring appears safe in clinical practice, although further improvements may be achieved through standardized contouring guidelines and harmonization strategies.

articles.title: Sexual dysfunction in men after radiotherapy for squamous cell carcinoma of the Anus: A danish anal cancer group DACG study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sexual dysfunction, particularly erectile dysfunction (ED), is well documented after pelvic radiotherapy, but evidence in men with squamous cell carcinoma of the anus (SCCA) remains sparse. PURPOSE: To assess erectile and ejaculatory function, and sexual interest up to five years after curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA, based on physician-graded toxicity and validated patient-reported outcomes (PROs). METHODS: This sub-study of the prospective DACG-I cohort (NCT05570279) included men treated with curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA (2015-2020). PROs (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-CR29) and physician-graded toxicity (CTCAE v4.0) were collected at baseline, 1, 3, and 5-years. Symptom prevalences were described descriptively. Longitudinal changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models on linearly transformed EORTC scores. RESULTS: Of 80 enrolled men, baseline data were available for 76. At baseline, majority were symptom-free. Erectile and ejaculatory dysfunction emerged mainly within 1-3 years after treatment and persisted through 5 years. For the total cohort, ejaculatory dysfunction increased from 4.5% at baseline to 12.3% at 3 years. Physician-assessed ED (NCI-CTCAE grade ≥ 2) increased from 11.9% to 39.3% at 3 years. PROs indicated greater deterioration in erectile function at parallel time points. EORTC scores confirmed moderate-to-major clinically important deterioration at 1 and 3 years. Sexual interest remained stable over time. CONCLUSION: Sexual dysfunction, particularly ED, represents an increasingly prevalent and persistent late adverse effect in men treated with curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA. The early onset of symptoms and the limited extent of recovery underscore the need for structured assessment based on PROs to support timely identification and supportive care.

articles.title: Carbon ion radiotherapy for non-metastatic pancreatic cancer: final results of the prospective phase 2 PACK-study (NCT04194268).
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) in patients with non-metastatic, inoperable pancreatic cancer in a prospective phase 2 setting. METHODS: In this single-center investigator-initiated phase 2 trial, 25 patients with locally advanced or locally recurrent pancreatic cancer were included. CIRT was performed using an intensity-controlled rasterscanning system for beam application [total dose: 48 Gy (RBE), 12 fractions]. Concurrent chemotherapy with Gemcitabine 300 mg/m2 was administered weekly. The primary endpoint was the 1-year OS rate, defined as time from study inclusion. 1y- and 2y-OS and -PFS were calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method, 95 % confidence intervals are shown. Toxicity was evaluated using CTCAEv5.0. RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were included in the final analysis. After the completed 12-month follow-up of the last patient, the 1- and 2-year OS rates were 78 % [CI 63 %; 97 %] and 59 % [CI 41 %; 84 %]. The median OS was 26.5 months. The 1- and 2-year PFS rates were 26 % [CI 13 %; 52 %] and 10 % [CI 3 %; 37 %] with a median PFS of 8.1 months. Study treatment was well tolerated with three treatment-related CTCAE grade 3 toxicities, including one case of abdominal pain, one upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage and one ureteric stricture. No treatment-related CTCAE grade 4-5 toxicities were observed. CONCLUSION: Chemoradiation with carbon ions demonstrated encouraging overall survival and acceptable toxicity in non-metastatic pancreatic cancer patients. A subsequent randomized Phase 3 trial should investigate OS superiority of CIRT compared to conventional chemoradiotherapy or chemotherapy.

articles.title: Synchronous Percutaneous Biopsy and Cryoablation for Suspicious Solitary Pulmonary Nodules.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and safety of synchronous CT-guided core needle biopsy and cryoablation for highly suspicious 1-2 cm pulmonary nodules MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 102 consecutive patients undergoing synchronous CT-guided core needle biopsy and cryoablation between August 2020 and October 2025. Treatment was undertaken on the basis of clinical and imaging suspicion before final histopathologic diagnosis. A cryoprobe was placed before biopsy to provide an intraprocedural landmark. Technical success, diagnostic yield, and adverse events were evaluated in all 102 patients; local tumor progression and overall survival were evaluated separately in 81 patients with pathology-confirmed NSCLC. RESULTS: Cryoablation technical success was 100% (102/102), and concurrent biopsy diagnostic yield was 87.3% (89/102). Biopsy identified 86 malignant diagnoses, including 81 NSCLCs. Mean nodule diameter was 1.52 ± 0.30 cm. Median follow-up in the NSCLC cohort was 34.5 months (IQR, 18.4-49.4 months). The cumulative incidence of recorded local tumor progression was 8.8% at both 1 and 3 years, and overall survival was 100% and 90.8%, respectively. Pneumothorax requiring chest tube drainage occurred in 20.6% (21/102), and no procedure-related deaths were reported. CONCLUSION: The synchronous biopsy and cryoablation approach was technically feasible and provided a specific histopathologic diagnosis in 87.3% of selected patients with highly suspicious 1.0-2.0-cm pulmonary nodules. Among patients with pathology-confirmed NSCLC, local-control outcomes were within the range reported in similar cryoablation-only series.

articles.title: Structural brain correlates of symptom severity in stress-induced exhaustion.
articles.abstract: Exhaustion due to chronic stress, a hallmark feature of burnout, represents a substantial and growing public health burden, yet its structural brain correlates remain poorly understood. We used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to examine associations between regional gray matter volume and symptom severity in a cohort of 300 individuals on self-reported sick leave due to the Swedish medical condition stress-induced exhaustion disorder (ED), characterized by debilitating fatigue following prolonged stress exposure. Symptom severity was assessed using the Shirom-Melamed Burnout Questionnaire (SMBQ-18) and its subscales. Overall symptom severity (SMBQ-18 total score) and Physical Exhaustion (PE) were negatively associated with gray matter volume in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a region implicated in stress regulation and affective control, which remained significant when adjusting for depressive symptoms. An exploratory finding was that Listlessness was negatively associated with gray matter volume in the bilateral hippocampi and right middle temporal gyrus after adjustment for depressive symptoms. These results provide evidence from a large cohort for brain-symptom associations in chronic stress and highlight the value of dimensional approaches for capturing heterogeneity in stress-related conditions.

articles.title: Hardware ray-traced optical-photon Monte Carlo for radiation detector simulation: a TOPAS extension on Apple Silicon.
articles.abstract: Optical-photon Monte Carlo (MC) underlies scintillator dosimetry, Cherenkov imaging and other medical-physics applications, yet Geant4 transport of the 105-106optical photons per event on the central processing unit (CPU) makes dataset-scale studies impractical even on a multi-core workstation. We implement and verify a hardware ray-tracing optical-photon transport extension for TOPAS on Apple Silicon.Approach. Charged-particle transport remains in Geant4 on the CPU, where the extension computes the scintillation and Cherenkov yields. Optical-photon generation, propagation and scoring run on the graphics processing unit (GPU), which finds boundaries with its ray-tracing hardware or, for curved solids, by solving the surface equation. The optical processes follow their Geant4 counterparts, with the dielectric-dielectric boundary physics algebraically identical. We verify the extension with ten benchmarks (B1-B10), covering optical physics, detector-chain timing and curved-surface intersection, on an Apple M3 Ultra with an 80-core GPU and a 30-thread CPU baseline.Main results. Every verification endpoint passes the equivalence test declared in advance, with margins of ±1 % in fluence and ±1 percentage point in the reflection and transmission probabilities. The largest mean summed-fluence deviation is 0.147 %, and every summed-fluence 95 % confidence interval lies within ±1 %. The scintillation-reflector-wavelength-shifting chain agrees to -0.02 % and the curved-geometry imaging chain to -0.07 %, and the intersection study reproduces the geometric chords of whole solids within a 0.5 mm tolerance. The matched scintillator-lens-camera simulation runs 15.7-32.0 times faster in execution time and about 24 times faster end to end at 105events.Significance. The extension reproduces the analytical or CPU-Geant4 reference process by process within these margins, while accelerating matched transport by more than an order of magnitude. TOPAS scripts gain GPU acceleration without user-written C++, enabling dataset-scale generation of scintillation-dosimetry training sets and Cherenkov-imaging forward models on a single workstation.&#xD.

articles.title: Scatter correction for multi-source linear static CT via a geometry-aware parameter regression network with differentiable forward modeling.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Multi-source linear static CT (SLCT) offers high temporal resolution and a compact form factor by eliminating mechanical rotation. However, lateral offsets of peripheral X-ray beams break the rotational symmetry assumed by conventional scatter correction methods, resulting in location-dependent and asymmetric scatter point spread functions (PSFs). APPROACH: To address this challenge, we propose a scatter correction framework that integrates a geometry-aware analytical kernel with a parameter regression network (GAPR-Net). An explicit correction term is incorporated into the conventional cone-beam scatter kernel to model asymmetric PSF distortion induced by lateral source offsets. GAPR-Net learns scatter kernel hyperparameters associated with source geometry and object thickness from Monte Carlo pencil-beam data, while a differentiable forward model analytically estimates scatter and enables stable optimization under a geometric consistency loss. MAIN RESULTS: Extensive simulation experiments were performed using water, electron-density, and ICRP phantoms, together with a DICOM-derived head phantom reconstructed using the derived three-dimensional SLCT reconstruction algorithm. Compared with SKS, DSE, ResNet, and a static-CT-specific 1D U-Net, GAPR-Net achieved consistent improvements. For the electron-density and ICRP phantoms, GAPR-Net achieved scatter-estimation mean absolute percentage errors of 4.43% and 5.31%, respectively. In the reconstructed images, it achieved a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 29.51 dB for the electron-density phantom and reduced the mean absolute percentage error of the ICRP thorax phantom from 14.69% to 6.07%. Head-phantom experiments at 80 kVp, 100 kVp, and 120 kVp further demonstrated stable performance across different X-ray spectra. A physical testbed experiment was conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed GAPR-Net under real conditions. SIGNIFICANCE: GAPR-Net provides a physically interpretable and computationally efficient approach for correcting non-stationary asymmetric scatter artifacts in SLCT.&#xD.

articles.title: Spot-wise compensation of proton beam deflection and radiation field deformation in the transverse magnetic field of an in-beam MR scanner using a research version of a commercial treatment planning system.
articles.abstract: ObjectiveMagnetic resonance-integrated proton therapy (MRiPT) offers the potential for high-precision, image-guided particle therapy but is challenged by magnetic field (MF)-induced proton beam deflection and radiation field deformation. Unless compensated for, these effects compromise dose conformity and prohibit clinical implementation. This work aims to develop and experimentally validate a spot-wise compensation method capable of restoring proton dose distributions in the presence of a measured 3D magnetic vector field map within a clinical treatment planning system (TPS).ApproachA spot-wise compensation framework was implemented in a research version of RayStation, a TPS commercially available for clinical use. The method compensates both lateral beam deflection and MF-induced radiation field deformation by shifting individual pencil-beam spots based on displacement vectors derived from dose calculations in water phantoms using the measured MF of an in-beam MR scanner integrated with a horizontal proton beamline. Two complementary strategies were implemented: a patient-specific approach based on plan-specific displacement calculations, and a generic approach using precomputed displacement maps derived from a reference phantom. Compensation performance was evaluated in representative clinical cases. Dose distributions were experimentally validated using 2D ionisation chamber array measurements.Main ResultsBoth compensation methods effectively restored target coverage, dose homogeneity, and organ-at-risk sparing to the level of no-MF reference plans. The patient-specific method generally achieved a higher performance, whereas the generic compensation method enabled rapid automated correction with sufficient accuracy for clinical workflows involving deep-seated tumours. Local γ-analysis demonstrated excellent agreement between measured and calculated doses, with pass rates exceeding 98.5% for 3%/3 mm criteria.SignificanceThis work demonstrates that compensation of MF-induced proton beam deflection and field deformation can be achieved entirely within a research version of the RayStation TPS using measured, MR scanner-specific MF data. The proposed method provides a scalable, robust framework for future MRiPT clinical applications.&#xD.

articles.title: Toward truly agentic radiology AI: A multimodal architecture framework and differentiated implementation roadmap.
articles.abstract: Agentic artificial intelligence(AI) represents a structural transition from task-specific tools to autonomous systems capable of goal-oriented, multi-step reasoning. However, translating this potential into radiology requires a fundamental shift from text-dominated architectures to avision-first approachthat engages the specialty's diagnostic core. In this paper, we characterize the multimodal challenge distinguishing radiology from text-centric domains, where high-dimensional images serve as the primary diagnostic substrate rather than supplementary data. We reviewthree image-text coupling architectures, their clinical capabilities, limitations, and deployment feasibility. These include output-level coupling through sequential image-text pipelines, representation-level coupling through contrastive aligned dual encoders, and token-level coupling through generative vision-language models. To guide development, we introduce afive-level taxonomy of autonomy(Levels 1-5), establishing clear validation checkpoints and regulatory expectations for increasing machine independence, from text-based workflow automation to fully autonomous closed-loop systems. We emphasize that interoperability via standardized protocols, includingDICOMweb, HL7-FHIR, Model Context Protocol (MCP), and Agent2Agent (A2A), is as critical as the AI models themselves. Finally, we address critical implementation guardrails, including mitigatingalgorithmic hallucinations, defending againstadversarial prompt injection, and preserving human diagnostic proficiency amidst the risk of AI-induced skill decay. This comprehensive roadmap provides a structured path for integrating autonomous visual reasoning into modern medical imaging environments.

articles.title: One-shot dual imaging: simultaneous visualization of bone and nerve structures using modified DIXON and fast field echo resembling computed tomography with restricted echo-spacing magnetic resonance imaging.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Simultaneous evaluation of osseous and neural structures is important in assessing lumbar spine pathologies. However, conventional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences cannot depict both structures simultaneously, and multiple sequences may prolong scanning time and cause spatial misregistration. This preliminary feasibility study investigated whether modified Dixon (mDIXON, Philips Healthcare)-assisted fast field echo resembling computed tomography using restricted echo-spacing (FRACTURE, Philips Healthcare) enabled simultaneous depiction of both structures from a single acquisition. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this single-center prospective study, healthy volunteers underwent lumbar spine MRI using a 1.5-T MRI system. Bone (in-phase) and nerve (water) images obtained using mDIXON-assisted FRACTURE (3D-mDIXON) were compared with conventional FRACTURE and 3D-FFE-ProSet (3D-ProSet), respectively. Image performance was evaluated using the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and visual assessment. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test was used to compare CNR and visual assessment scores. Interobserver agreement was assessed according to the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC[A,2]). RESULTS: Twenty healthy volunteers (mean age, 48.2 ± 9.6 years) were included. For bone evaluation, the CNR was significantly higher with 3D-mDIXON (in-phase) than with FRACTURE (p < 0.01). For nerve evaluation, CNR did not significantly differ between 3D-mDIXON (water) and 3D-ProSet. However, the overall preference score (p < 0.01) and motion artifact score (p < 0.01) were significantly higher for 3D-mDIXON than for 3D-ProSet. CONCLUSIONS: The 3D-mDIXON technique enables the simultaneous depiction of both structures from a single acquisition while maintaining adequate image quality. This approach may improve imaging efficiency and facilitate assessment of their spatial relationship.

articles.title: Radiologists' and radiographers' considerations regarding the implementation of targeted ultrasound as primary imaging modality in patients with focal breast complaints: A concept mapping study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Emerging evidence indicates that breast ultrasound can function as an effective stand-alone diagnostic tool for focal breast complaints, with digital breast tomosynthesis (DBT) reserved for inconclusive cases. This study identifies and prioritizes radiologists' and radiographers' professional considerations regarding an ultrasound-first approach. METHODS: Using digital concept mapping, radiologists and radiographers independently generated, categorized, and rated statements related to the implementation of ultrasound as the initial modality. Thematic clusters were derived and prioritized based on participant ratings (7-point scale). RESULTS: Radiologists produced 43 statements across seven clusters: 1) Diagnostic accuracy, 2) Logistics and planning, 3) Communication, 4) Guidelines, 5) Patient satisfaction, 6) Age and screening, and 7) Accessibility of approach, prioritizing the clusters Diagnostic accuracy (rating 5.41), Guidelines (rating 5.21), and Logistics and planning (rating 4.88). Radiographers produced 35 statements in four clusters: 1) Communication, 2) Logistics and planning, 3) Organization and responsibilities, and 4) Patient satisfaction, placing greatest emphasis on the clusters Organization and responsibilities (rating 4.91) and Communication (rating 4.74). These patterns indicate that radiologists primarily emphasized diagnostic and clinical feasibility, whereas radiographers focused more on operational and role-related considerations. CONCLUSION: Radiologists and radiographers identified both shared and profession-specific considerations related to an ultrasound-first approach. Differences in prioritized themes reflect distinct professional roles and highlight the complexity of changing established imaging pathways. These findings may inform future research and implementation efforts by drawing attention to profession-specific considerations relevant to the adoption of such pathways.

articles.title: Diagnostic value of breast MRI and Kaiser score in BIRADS 0 and 4 lesions compared with histopathology and follow-up.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Breast cancer is the most frequently diagnosed cancer type in women, and early detection and treatment significantly improve survival rates. In conventional imaging methods (mammography and ultrasound), lesions classified as BI-RADS 0 or 4 often lead to a high rate of unnecessary biopsies, resulting in both superfluous invasive procedures for patients and increased costs for the healthcare system. The aim of our study is to investigate the diagnostic validity of the Kaiser score in predicting malignancy in patients who underwent breast MRI following inconclusive or suspicious findings (BI-RADS 0 or 4) on conventional imaging, based on pathology results or clinical follow-up. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Between September 2022 and April 2024, 99 patients who underwent breast MRI due to inconclusive results from conventional breast imaging methods (mammography and breast ultrasound) or the detection of suspicious findings (BI-RADS 0 or 4), and who had either histopathological evaluation following biopsy under US or MG guidance or were followed for at least 12 months, were included in this single-center retrospective study. The 99 patients included in the study were divided into two groups based on histopathology or follow-up outcomes (benign lesion group and malignant lesion group). Comparisons were made between these two groups. RESULTS: When comparing benign and malignant groups, statistically significant differences were observed for age (p < 0,001), age at menarche (p = 0,004), breastfeeding status (p = 0,009), menopausal status (p = 0,017), and use of hormone replacement therapy (p = 0,036). MRI BI-RADS (p < 0,001) and Kaiser scores (p < 0,001) were notably higher in the malignant group. Kaiser score was identified as the strongest diagnostic predictor of malignancy (AUC = 0,977, 95 % CI: 0.955-0.999; p < 0,001). Using a cut-off value of Kaiser score > 5, the sensitivity and specificity were 97 % (95 % CI: 84.2 %-99.9 %) and 87.9 % (95 % CI: 77.5 %-94.6 %), respectively. The MRI BI-RADS ranked second with a cut-off value > 4 (AUC = 0.878, 95 % CI: 0.805-0.950; p < 0.001); at this threshold, the sensitivity and specificity were 60.6 % (95 % CI: 42.1 %-77.1 %) and 100 % (95 % CI: 94.6 %-100.0 %), respectively. In multivariable logistic regression, higher Kaiser score (OR = 4.25, p < 0.001) and older age (OR = 1.16, p = 0.041) were associated with higher odds of malignancy, whereas older age at menarche was associated with lower odds (OR = 0.347, p = 0.030). CONCLUSION: For breast lesions classified as BI-RADS 0 or 4 on conventional imaging, the Kaiser score provides excellent diagnostic accuracy and may support lesion stratification when used with MRI BI-RADS assessment; biopsy decisions should remain based on integrated clinical and imaging findings.

articles.title: CT low attenuation area quantification versus visual scoring for early pulmonary emphysema detection in lung cancer screening.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare low-attenuation analysis (LAA) with visual scoring and explore their application in the detection of emphysema in low-dose CT (LDCT) scans. METHODS: A random cohort of 352 CT examinations from health-check participants was selected from a lung cancer screening(LCS) dataset. Scans were evaluated for emphysema by four readers according to latest Fleischner criteria, and emphysema was quantified by LAA with thresholds from -900 HU to -980 HU. Fleiss' Kappa assessed inter-reader agreement on visual detection and severity classification. Cases with full agreement on emphysema presence were used to compare LAA quantification and visual detection. Spearman correlation test measured their correlation and Cohen's Kappa evaluated the agreement between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection. RESULTS: Agreement among four observers was found in 266 cases on emphysema presence based on visual evaluation (K = 0.738, 0.737-0.739). Concordance between emphysema presence using a LAA% cutoff of 6% and binary visual classification was 61.3% (163/266, Cohen's Kappa:0.173. Spearman analysis showed a correlation between LAA% and visual scores (P < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: LAA emphysema quantification shows in comparison with visual scoring limited performance for discrimination of normal and emphysematous lung parenchyma in a Low dose CT Lung cancer screening dataset. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Full agreement among four readers regarding visual emphysema classification was achieved in only three-quarters of cases. Limited concordance was found between LAA%-measured emphysema and visual detection.

articles.title: Dissociable associations of free-water fraction and DTI-ALPS index with disease manifestation and mutation carrier status in Parkinson's disease.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a biologically heterogeneous disorder. Diffusion MRI-derived free-water fraction (FWf) and DTI-ALPS index have been proposed as biomarkers of PD-related brain alterations; however, their relationships with clinical disease manifestation and genetic susceptibility remain unclear. This study investigated whether substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc) FWf and DTI-ALPS indices show different associations with disease status and mutation carrier status across the PD continuum. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Diffusion MRI data from the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative were analyzed, including healthy controls (HCs), non-manifesting mutation carriers (NMCs), and patients with sporadic or genetic PD. A 2 × 2 factorial analysis of covariance was performed to assess the effects of disease status and mutation carrier status on SNc FWf and DTI-ALPS indices. Exploratory longitudinal associations between baseline imaging measures and 4-year clinical outcomes were examined using multivariable linear regression with adjustment for the corresponding baseline clinical measures. RESULTS: Among 284 participants (63 HCs, 48 NMCs, 126 sporadic PD patients, and 47 genetic PD patients), mean SNc FWf showed a significant main effect of disease status, whereas mutation carrier status and the interaction effect were not significant. Sporadic PD patients exhibited higher SNc FWf than HCs and NMCs. In contrast, the left-sided DTI-ALPS index was associated with mutation carrier status. NMCs had lower left-sided DTI-ALPS indices than HCs and sporadic PD patients. In the exploratory longitudinal analysis, higher baseline mean SNc FWf was associated with a higher 4-year MDS-UPDRS Part II score, although this association was not significant when the analysis was restricted to participants with manifest PD. CONCLUSIONS: SNc FWf and DTI-ALPS may capture complementary aspects of PD heterogeneity. SNc FWf appears more closely related to clinical disease expression, whereas DTI-ALPS index may reflect differences associated with genetic susceptibility. Further validation in larger mutation-stratified and longitudinal cohorts is warranted.

articles.title: Utility of super-resolution deep-learning reconstruction for improving visibility of hepatocellular carcinoma at hepatic dynamic CT: comparison with hybrid iterative reconstruction and conventional deep-learning reconstruction.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to evaluate whether Precise IQ Engine (PIQE), a super-resolution deep-learning reconstruction designed to enhance spatial resolution while reducing image noise using a deep convolutional neural network, improves the visibility of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) compared with hybrid iterative reconstruction (Adaptive Iterative Dose Reduction with three-dimensional processing [AIDR 3D]) and conventional deep-learning reconstruction (Advanced Intelligent Clear-IQ Engine [AiCE]) in hepatic dynamic CT. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We evaluated 64 patients with HCC who had undergone hepatic dynamic CT. Hepatic arterial- and equilibrium phase (HAP and EP) scans were reconstructed with AIDR, AiCE, and PIQE. A radiologist measured the standard deviation of attenuation in the liver parenchyma as the image noise and calculated the contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) = (ROIT - ROIL)/N in HAP and (ROIL - ROIT)/N in EP. ROIL is the mean attenuation of the liver parenchyma, ROIT the mean tumor attenuation, and N the noise. HCC visibility was assessed by 2 additional radiologists and graded with a focus on tumor margin delineation on a 5-point confidence scale. RESULTS: PIQE showed the lowest image noise, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). The CNR of HCCs was highest with PIQE, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). Qualitative visibility scores for HCCs were also highest with PIQE, followed by AiCE and AIDR, in both HAP and EP (all p < 0.01). CONCLUSION: PIQE significantly improves HCC visibility compared with AIDR and AiCE in hepatic dynamic CT, along with reduced image noise and increased CNR.

articles.title: Quantitative intraoperative assessment of fronto-orbital advancement and remodelling in craniosynostosis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Intraoperative morphometric analysis provides immediate feedback for evaluating surgical outcomes in infants with craniosynostosis undergoing fronto-orbital advancement and remodelling. However, current intraoperative assessment primarily relies on surgeon's judgement and clinical experience. This study aimed to develop a computational method for comprehensive analysis of detailed morphological features in the intraoperative 3D surface scan acquired with a structured-light handheld scanner. METHODS: Our method consists of three stages: First, we computed cephalometric measurements, such as interfrontal angle (IFA) and cranial index (CI). Second, we developed a coarse-to-fine registration method to align the pre- and intraoperative surfaces, enabling accurate superimposition of non-operated region. Finally, we employed geometric morphometrics to examine frontal morphological shape differences. The proposed method was applied to one patient with trigonocephaly and one with Saethre-Chotzen syndrome (SCS). RESULTS: A small root mean square error (0.5-0.6 mm) indicated high registration accuracy. The cephalometric measurements and colour maps of intraoperative geometric changes indicated frontal advancement in both the anterior and lateral directions, with an increased IFA in the trigonocephaly case and a decreased CI in the SCS case. Geometric morphometric analysis suggested that the central forehead remained relatively flat on the intraoperative 3D surface, although the overall frontal morphology approached that of the control group. CONCLUSION: The proposed analytical method combined with 3D scanning provides new insights into quantitative intraoperative assessment through the comparison of cephalometric measurements, quantification of geometric surface changes, and examination of morphological variation. This framework has the potential to be integrated into routine surgical workflows for craniosynostosis treatment.
articles.journal: Int J Comput Assist Radiol Surg

articles.title: The relationship between chemical shift MRI findings and histological grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of percentage signal intensity (SI) drop on chemical-shift magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) for distinguishing Fuhrman grade 1 from Fuhrman grades 2-4 clear-cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 85 patients with histopathologically confirmed ccRCC who underwent preoperative 1.5-T MRI including chemical-shift sequences between 2016 and 2024. Percentage tumour-to-spleen SI drop was calculated from in-phase and opposed-phase images. Tumours were classified as Fuhrman grade 1 (n = 30) or Fuhrman grades 2-4 (n = 55), based on grades recorded in the original surgical pathology reports. MRI findings were compared between groups, and ROC curve analysis was performed to evaluate the discriminatory performance of percentage SI drop. RESULTS: Percentage SI drop was significantly greater in Fuhrman grade 1 tumours than in Fuhrman grades 2-4 tumours [40.0% (IQR, 25.4-54.2) vs. 17.4% (IQR, 5.9-29.2); p = 0.003]. Fuhrman grades 2-4 tumours were significantly larger than grade 1 tumours [46 mm (IQR, 28-74) vs. 39 mm (IQR, 30-49); p = 0.01], whereas tumour composition did not differ significantly (p = 0.08). ROC analysis showed modest discriminatory performance (AUC, 0.695; 95% CI, 0.566-0.824; p = 0.003). A percentage SI drop cut-off of ≥ 27.8% yielded 66.7% sensitivity and 67.3% specificity for identifying Fuhrman grade 1 tumours. CONCLUSION: Percentage SI drop was greater in Fuhrman grade 1 than in Fuhrman grades 2-4 ccRCCs, but discrimination was modest and incremental value beyond tumour size was not established. These findings are limited to an exploratory comparison using historical Fuhrman grades and cannot be extrapolated to contemporary World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grading.

articles.title: Dual-layer spectral CT-derived iodine and extracellular volume biomarkers for noninvasive assessment of hepatic fibrosis in Fontan-associated liver disease.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived normalized iodine concentration and extracellular volume fraction for noninvasive assessment of hepatic fibrosis in patients with Fontan-associated liver disease. METHODS: This single-center exploratory retrospective study included 23 patients with Fontan-associated liver disease who underwent both liver biopsy and delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT between January 2021 and December 2023. Normalized iodine concentration was calculated as hepatic iodine concentration divided by aortic iodine concentration. Hematocrit-adjusted extracellular volume fraction (ECV) was calculated from delayed-phase iodine-density maps. Histologic fibrosis stage based on the METAVIR system was used as the reference standard. Associations between CT biomarkers and fibrosis stage were assessed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test, and Spearman correlation. Diagnostic performance for advanced fibrosis (≥ F3) and cirrhosis (F4) was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis. RESULTS: Histologic fibrosis stages were F1 in 4 patients, F2 in 2, F3 in 9, and F4 in 8. ECV was higher in advanced fibrosis stages, with median values of 39.21% in F1, 37.15% in F2, 42.72% in F3, and 46.78% in F4. ECV differed significantly among fibrosis stages (p = 0.014), showed a significant ordered trend (p < 0.001), and correlated positively with histologic stage (ρ = 0.666, p < 0.001). IC-normalized showed a weak positive correlation with fibrosis stage, but the ordered trend did not reach statistical significance. For advanced fibrosis, ECV showed promising preliminary discrimination, with an AUC of 0.902 (95% CI, 0.766-1.000). For cirrhosis, ECV showed an AUC of 0.833 (95% CI, 0.655-1.000), with sensitivity of 87.5%, specificity of 80.0%, and negative predictive value of 92.3% at a cutoff of 43.45%. CONCLUSION: In this single-center exploratory study, delayed-phase dual-layer spectral CT-derived ECV showed a significant association with histologic fibrosis severity and promising preliminary discrimination for advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis in Fontan-associated liver disease. External validation in larger, independent Fontan cohorts is required before clinical application.

articles.title: An interpretable contrast-enhanced CT-based cross-attention transformer model for predicting progression-free survival in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: a multicenter study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) typically have a dismal prognosis, even after undergoing radical cystectomy (RC). To address this limitation, we constructed and evaluated a preoperative deep learning (DL) model that leverages computed tomography (CT) imaging to stratify MIBC patients according to their risk of postoperative disease progression. METHODS: Data from MIBC patients undergoing RC at one of four institutions were retrospectively analyzed and allocated to training and validation cohorts. A dual-channel information fusion DL model was developed to predict the postoperative risk of progression according to preoperative CT images. Subsequently, a DL-based clinical signature was created by combining clinical features with the DL-derived score. The concordance index (C-index) and area under the curve (AUC) were used to evaluate the DL model's predictive capability, which was compared with the DL-based clinical signature, a clinical model, and a Ki67 model. RESULTS: In the retrospective cohort of 427 patients with MIBC, the DL score demonstrated favorable predictive performance for disease progression in the validation cohort (C-index: 0.774; AUC: 0.785), and generally showed higher predictive performance than the comparator models in the validation cohort. Using an optimal threshold, the patient cohort was categorized into two distinct subgroups, high-risk and low-risk, with differences in the cumulative incidence of progression observed between the two groups, supporting the model's ability to stratify patients according to progression risk. CONCLUSIONS: The utilization of preoperative CT imaging in a DL framework enabled PFS prediction and risk stratification in patients with MIBC, with potential value for individualized postoperative surveillance.

articles.title: Deep learning-based detection of pneumoperitoneum on computed tomography: performance and clinical feasibility.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Early detection of pneumoperitoneum on computed tomography (CT) is critical because delayed diagnosis of gastrointestinal perforation is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. We evaluated the diagnostic performance and clinical applicability of a deep learning model for automated pneumoperitoneum detection on CT. METHODS: In this retrospective diagnostic accuracy study, CT scans for 263 patients with surgically confirmed gastrointestinal perforation and 78 normal controls from a single tertiary center (January 2010-September 2024) were included. Positive CT scans were divided into training, validation, internal test, and temporally independent external test datasets, with 78 normal controls included in the external test dataset. Free air was manually segmented and verified by surgical and radiological experts. A segmentation-based deep learning model was developed using the no-new-Segment Anything Model (nnSAM) framework and compared with a conventional no-new-Net (nnUNet) model. Segmentation and classification performance were assessed on internal and temporally independent external test datasets. RESULT: In the internal test dataset (n = 43 positive cases), the nnSAM model achieved a higher detection rate (97.7% vs. 90.7%) and significantly higher mean Dice similarity coefficient (0.739 ± 0.266 vs. 0.684 ± 0.283; p = 0.045) than the nnUNet one. In the external test dataset, nnSAM also showed a higher detection rate in positive cases (97.9% vs. 85.4%) and a significantly higher mean Dice similarity coefficient (0.863 ± 0.189 vs. 0.746 ± 0.208; p = 0.003). CONCLUSION: The performance advantage of nnSAM was particularly evident in small-volume pneumoperitoneum cases. The nnSAM-based model showed improved accuracy and robustness for pneumoperitoneum detection on CT, supporting its potential as a clinically useful decision-support tool for emergency radiology workflows and triage of patients with suspected gastrointestinal perforation.

articles.title: CT assessment of colonic laterality in situs inversus and situs ambiguus: a multicenter retrospective study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize proximal and distal colonic laterality and appendiceal-base location on CT in patients with situs inversus and situs ambiguus. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 79 patients identified from abdominal CT reports at three tertiary hospitals between December 2003 and March 2025 (70 with situs inversus; 9 with situs ambiguus). A radiologist assessed thoracoabdominal organ arrangement, proximal and distal colonic laterality, combined proximal-distal colonic laterality pattern, and appendiceal-base location. The end of the cecum was used when the appendiceal base was not visible. Distributions of colonic laterality between the two situs types were compared using exact tests. RESULTS: In situs inversus, the proximal colon was left-sided in 66/70 patients (94.3%; 95% CI, 86.2-97.8), the distal colon was right-sided in 67/70 (95.7%; 95% CI, 88.1-98.5), and a left-proximal/right-distal combined colonic pattern occurred in 64/70 (91.4%; 95% CI, 82.5-96.0). The appendiceal base or cecal surrogate was in the left lower quadrant in 61/70 (87.1%; 95% CI, 77.3-93.1). In situs ambiguus, the proximal colon was midline-crossing in 7/9 patients (77.8%; 95% CI, 45.3-93.7), and the distal colon was left-sided in 6/9 (66.7%; 95% CI, 35.4-87.9). Locations of the appendiceal base or cecal surrogate were distributed across all abdominal regions. Distributions of segmental and combined colonic laterality differed between situs inversus and situs ambiguus (all exact p < .001). CONCLUSION: Situs inversus usually shows mirror-image colonic laterality and a left-lower-quadrant appendiceal base, but exceptions occur. In this cohort, situs ambiguus showed greater variability. Colonic laterality and appendiceal-base location should be directly assessed on CT rather than inferred from situs classification alone.

articles.title: Spiradenocarcinoma in Brooke-Spiegler syndrome: radiology-pathology correlation of synchronous benign and malignant dermal adnexal tumors.
articles.abstract: Spiradenocarcinoma is a rare dermal adnexal malignancy often arising from a pre-existing benign spiradenoma and may occur sporadically or in the setting of the autosomal dominant genodermatosis Brooke-Spiegler Syndrome (BSS). Imaging descriptions of spiradenoma and spiradenocarcinoma are scant, with no literature to date describing comparative imaging features of benign and malignant tumors to the best of our knowledge. We report a case of a 64-year-old patient with a rapidly enlarging right frontal scalp mass and a relatively indolent left parietal scalp mass in addition to innumerable small head and neck nodules. MRI for preoperative planning demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement and markedly reduced diffusion in both lesions, while 18F-FDG PET-CT showed marked FDG avidity (SUVmax = 16.3) in the frontal mass but mild uptake in the parietal mass (SUVmax = 2.1). Histopathology confirmed the frontal mass to be a low-grade spiradenocarcinoma and the left parietal lesion a benign spiradenoma. Genetic testing confirmed BSS. This case illustrates the clinical-radiologic-pathologic correlation of spiradenocarcinoma in the context of BSS, a rare clinical and radiologic mimic of NF1, and highlights that rapid growth and FDG avidity may help the reporting radiologist to differentiate spiradenocarcinoma from spiradenoma in patients with BSS.

articles.title: Imaging features of pituitary Crooke cell adenoma: a 13-case series.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Crooke cell adenoma (CCA) is a rare and aggressive subtype of pituitary neuroendocrine tumor (PitNET). This study aimed to characterize the imaging features of CCA. METHODS: Preoperative and postoperative follow-up MR images of 13 patients with CCA were retrospectively reviewed to characterize their imaging features in conjunction with clinical and pathological findings. RESULTS: Among the 13 CCAs, 8 (61.5%) were macroadenomas and 5 (38.5%) were microadenomas. On T1-weighted imaging, 12 tumors (92.3%) were isointense. On T2-weighted imaging, 6 (46.2%) were hyperintense, 4 (30.8%) were hypointense, and 3 (23.1%) were isointense. Macroadenomas were predominantly hyperintense (5/8) or isointense (3/8), whereas microadenomas were predominantly hypointense (4/5). Multiple microcystic changes were observed in 2 macroadenomas (15.4%). Mild contrast enhancement was observed in 10 tumors (76.9%). Knosp grade 1 was the most common pattern of parasellar extension (8/13, 61.5%). During postoperative follow-up of 2-39 months, tumor progression occurred in 4 patients (30.8%), all of whom had undergone subtotal resection. Retrospective review of their preoperative contrast-enhanced MRI showed reduced enhancement of the tumor-adjacent internal carotid artery wall (ICAW) in all four cases. CONCLUSION: CCA exhibits several imaging characteristics, particularly mild contrast enhancement and a tumor size-related T2-weighted signal pattern. Knosp grade 1 was the most frequent parasellar extension pattern. Reduced enhancement of the tumor-adjacent ICAW was observed in four cases with postoperative tumor progression; however, the clinical significance of this finding requires validation in larger cohorts with longer-term follow-up.

articles.title: Sylviocentral ratio: a novel magnetic resonance imaging marker for differentiating probable idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus from diffuse cerebral atrophy.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Probable idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (pNPH) is a potentially treatable neurological disorder that can be difficult to differentiate from diffuse cerebral atrophy because of overlapping clinical and imaging features. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a novel magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived marker, the sylviocentral ratio, for distinguishing pNPH from diffuse cerebral atrophy. METHODS: In this prospective study, 72 patients (36 with pNPH and 36 with diffuse cerebral atrophy) underwent routine brain MRI, with an additional sagittal 3D T2-weighted SPACE acquisition; axial and coronal reformatted images were generated from the volumetric dataset for standardized measurements. Sylvian fissure and central sulcus diameters were measured on these standardized images using predefined anatomical landmarks, and the sylviocentral ratio was calculated. RESULTS: The sylviocentral ratio was significantly higher in patients with pNPH than in those with diffuse cerebral atrophy (10.94 ± 4.67 vs. 2.86 ± 2.00, p < 0.001). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.953 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.896-0.994). A cut-off value of ≥ 5.3 yielded a sensitivity of 91.7% and a specificity of 94.4%. Diagnostic performance was comparable to the callosal angle (AUC = 0.951) and superior to the Evans index (AUC = 0.922). The sylviocentral ratio remained independently associated with pNPH after adjustment for age (p < 0.001). Interobserver agreement was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] = 0.94). CONCLUSION: The sylviocentral ratio is a practical, reproducible, and highly accurate MRI marker for differentiating pNPH from diffuse cerebral atrophy and may complement established imaging parameters in clinical assessment. Given the limited size of the age-matched cohort, validation in larger, ideally external cohorts is warranted before widespread clinical implementation.

articles.title: Learning global and local representations for generalized category discovery in neurodegenerative diseases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) has achieved notable success in closed-set classification of neurodegenerative diseases, but its performance degrades significantly in more realistic open-set settings, such as discovering rare or novel disease subtypes from unlabeled data that are not seen during training. PURPOSE: This study introduces, to our knowledge, the first framework for generalized category discovery (GCD) in neurodegenerative diseases using MRI. It aims to leverage labeled data from known categories to automatically identify novel categories within unlabeled datasets. METHODS: We propose a GCD framework integrating semi-supervised contrastive learning with global-local representation learning to jointly optimize feature learning. Globally, we enforce consistency between weakly augmented views of the same instance by aligning their similarity relationships with other embeddings in a support queue. Locally, we treat neighborhood embeddings from the support queue as positive pairs for cross-instance contrastive learning, enhancing fine-grained discrimination. This dual strategy results in a unified learning objective that is applicable to both labeled and unlabeled data, effectively narrowing the representation gap among semantically similar instances. RESULTS: We evaluate our method on a benchmark dataset comprising six neurodegenerative diseases, with over 1500 patient samples. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms representative state-of-the-art methods. Specifically, our method achieves 66.02% Accuracy and 60.59% Normalized Mutual Information on all categories, and 54.53% Accuracy and 16.67% Normalized Mutual Information on novel categories, surpassing existing state-of-the-art methods. CONCLUSIONS: Our framework underscores the model's robustness and its practical value in discovering new neurodegenerative disease conditions, highlighting its potential for advancing open-set diagnostic AI.
